article_content: Two sisters have been banned from a variety of high street stores after being identified as professional shoplifters. Khalida Ahmed, 36, and Nazia Haq, 32, dubbed 'shopaholics,' received criminal ASBOs after police stated they treated their thefts as a 'trade.' The sisters, from Blackburn, Lancashire, were repeatedly arrested for shoplifting clothing and food from stores including TK Maxx, Boots, Argos, and Marks & Spencer. Nazia Haq, 32, (left) and Khalida Ahmed, 36, (right) received criminal ASBOs and are banned from high street stores after being identified as professional shoplifters. Blackburn town centre, one of the areas the sisters are banned from entering. Ahmed has shoplifting convictions dating back ten years. On one occasion, when caught attempting to leave a Kwiksave store without paying for almost £150 worth of groceries, she left her seven-year-old child to take the blame. The pair were arrested again last June for stealing clothing from a Matalan store and food from a Farmfoods store in nearby Accrington. At Blackburn Magistrates' Court, Ahmed and Haq were warned they could face up to five years in jail if they violated the Criminal Antisocial Behaviour Order (CRASBO) by entering the specified high street stores. Ahmed, described as the more prolific shoplifter, is also banned from Asda, Tesco, Sainsbury’s, Morrisons, Aldi, Lidl, Farmfoods, Iceland, Boots, Argos, Marks & Spencer, Next, Matalan, Primark, Mothercare, B&M Bargains, Debenhams, Claire’s Accessories, Accessorize, Toys 'R' Us, and Smyths Toys in Blackburn, Darwen, Accrington, and Burnley. She and Haq are banned from Blackburn’s shopping area and the Townsmoor retail park for the next two years. The CRASBO differs from regular ASBOs because it is recorded on the sisters’ criminal records. A third sister, Rizwana Ahmed, 33, pleaded guilty to stealing clothes from Matalan but did not receive an ASBO as it was her first conviction. Sgt David Clarke of Lancashire Police said the CRASBO would be extended if Khalida and Nazia began 'plying their trade' further afield. The pair are banned from a host of shops, including Marks & Spencer, in Blackburn, Darwen, Accrington, and Burnley. He said, 'We hope it will be a nice Christmas present for the shopkeepers of Blackburn and the rest of East Lancashire from Lancashire Constabulary.' 'These women, especially Khalida Ahmed, are prolific shoplifters, and we hope these orders can dramatically reduce their offending.' It is believed Khalida Ahmed first started shoplifting in 2002 after her husband, a part-time taxi driver, had to take time off because his car engine needed replacing. She appeared in court in July of that year after pleading guilty to stealing 118 grocery items worth £147. That hearing was told that a customer shopping in Kwiksave, Blackburn, noticed Ahmed acting suspiciously and watched her. She was standing near the entrance and the customer heard her tell her seven-year-old son to fetch his dad and ask him to bring the money in. Ahmed then left through a side exit, and the man followed her, confronting her at the front of the shop and asking if she intended to pay for the trolley of goods she had. She ran off, and the shopper chased her, at which point Ahmed began screaming that she was being attacked. The man let go of her and took hold of the boy, and Ahmed ran off again. Last year, Haq was ordered to pay £40 costs for stealing £80 worth of Lucozade and frozen food from Farmfoods in Accrington. Both were then arrested in July for stealing from Matalan. Ahmed was also detained for shoplifting at Farmfoods and Argos. In the latest hearing, Ahmed received a conditional discharge for 24 months, and Haq received a conditional discharge for 12 months. They were both ordered to pay £100 compensation to Matalan. Rizwana received a conditional discharge for 12 months and was ordered to pay £100 compensation and £100 costs. Carl Gaffney, prosecuting, said Rizwana only had one previous conviction and had found herself in 'rum company.' He added, 'The other two are professional shoplifters as far as the prosecution are concerned.' Mr. Gaffney said Ahmed and Haq were aware that if there were further offenses in other towns, such as Bolton or Preston, the police would seek to extend the ASBO to cover those towns. He said, 'The ASBO is not a paper tiger; it is a court order. I say for their benefit that they will be ripe for custodial sentences if they breach these orders. This is very much a last chance saloon for them.' Scott Parker, defending, said his clients had been remanded in custody for eight days during the latest proceedings, which had acted as a 'wake-up call.'

article_content: A recent study based on national census data reveals that one in four individuals in the UK identifies as non-religious. The analysis indicates a decline in Christianity, with its followers increasingly belonging to older age groups, especially retirees. Many young adults, particularly young men, are seemingly abandoning religious faith altogether. Approximately 32 percent of individuals under the age of 25 report having no religious affiliation. Since 2001, the number of Christians in Britain has decreased by 4.1 million. This period also saw a rise in atheism, coinciding with challenges faced by churches due to equality laws and secular movements. Islam, the UK's second-largest religion, has also faced scrutiny due to the actions of extremist groups. The 2011 census showed a decline in the Christian population to 33.2 million, with only about one-third regularly attending church services outside of major life events. Conversely, the number of people identifying as non-religious increased by 45 percent between 2001 and 2011, reaching 14.1 million in 2011. The Office for National Statistics noted that while the decline in religious affiliation is most prominent among young people, there is an increase in the percentage of individuals reporting no religion across all age groups. A significant majority (over 90%) of those identifying as non-religious are white individuals born in Britain. This group also represents the highest proportion of employed individuals compared to religious groups. The city with the most significant decline in religious belief is Norwich, where 42.5 percent of the population identifies as non-religious. However, more than half of individuals under 25 in certain areas such as Norwich, Brighton and Hove (England), and Blaenau Gwent, Caerphilly, and Rhondda Cynon Taf (Wales) report having no religious affiliation. In contrast, Knowsley on Merseyside is the most Christian area in England and Wales, with 81 percent of residents identifying as Christian.

article_content: At the European Youth Boxing Championships in Croatia, boxer Vido Loncar shockingly assaulted the referee following his defeat. During a match where Loncar faced Algirdas Baniulis, the referee intervened, resulting in a standing count against Loncar before stopping the fight. As both boxers awaited the announcement of Baniulis's victory, Loncar, a light-heavyweight, launched a violent attack on the referee, continuing even after the official fell. Baniulis, from Lithuania, quickly left as spectators were stunned by the attack. Loncar's coach did not step in as the assault unfolded, and security personnel eventually dragged Loncar from the ring. The referee received immediate medical assistance. It was clear that Algirdas Baniulis of Lithuania was comfortably ahead before the match was halted. Loncar was visibly upset by the stoppage at the European Youth Championships. Subsequently, he unleashed a series of blows on the referee until security intervened. After the brutal attack, Loncar was pulled from the ring, and the referee was aided to his feet.

article_content: Today's uncertain economy presents challenges for leaders navigating their workforce through this turbulence. Effective leadership is crucial for an organization's success. However, leadership development (LD) approaches vary significantly, including in-house training, third-party external support, formal education, and even the traditional “sink or swim” method. LHH, a talent solutions provider, sought to gauge the future of leadership development. They surveyed 1,502 C-level executives in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and Australia about their LD challenges, identifying five key issues. Five LD Challenges Executives Are Facing: Investing In An Internal Culture Of Development I spoke with Kristen Leverone, managing director of LD at LHH. She stated via email that the current economic uncertainty challenges C-suite leaders tasked with guiding their workforce through the turbulence. Leverone highlighted the survey's finding that 89% of executives consider “agility and responding to constant change” a significant challenge, adding that it is demanding. “It’s clear that a business's health, particularly in the current environment, is closely tied to workforce investment. C-suite leaders largely agree that reskilling workers (76%), recruitment and retention (79%), and managing remote workers (79%) will become increasingly important in the future of work,” she noted. “However, when implementing internal development programs, leaders struggle to ensure employees utilize available resources and dedicate time to their professional growth.” The report recognizes that change management and change leadership skills are not innate. It quotes Dr. Joshua Margolis, Chair of Harvard Business School’s leadership development program, who said, “It’s imperative for leaders to understand the shifting terrain around them to ensure their organizations' ongoing relevance and sustainability.” Leverone advises clients to invest in building an internal culture of development where workers can take ownership and advance their careers through learning experiences that provide the specific skills they seek. “This means thinking beyond individual training programs and encouraging employees to continuously learn and improve, ideally in a collaborative environment where they can share their knowledge,” she explained. “This mindset should start at the top, with leaders recognizing and celebrating employees who develop themselves, encouraging others to follow suit. Leadership development thrives when it is a two-way, participatory process that incorporates the next generation’s views on DEI, CSR, and skills.” Leverone emphasizes that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to LD. She concludes, “It’s important to understand what works for your company and help clients find solutions that best suit their specific needs.”
translated_content: L'économie incertaine d'aujourd'hui présente des défis pour les dirigeants qui doivent guider leurs équipes à travers ces turbulences. Un leadership efficace est crucial pour le succès d'une organisation. Cependant, les approches de développement du leadership (DL) varient considérablement, incluant la formation en interne, le soutien externe de consultants, la formation diplômante, et même la méthode traditionnelle du « se débrouiller ou disparaître ». LHH, un fournisseur de solutions de talents, a cherché à évaluer l'avenir du développement du leadership. Ils ont interrogé 1 502 cadres de direction (niveau C) aux États-Unis, au Canada, au Royaume-Uni et en Australie au sujet de leurs défis en matière de DL, identifiant cinq enjeux majeurs. Cinq défis en matière de DL auxquels les dirigeants sont confrontés : investir dans une culture interne de développement. Je me suis entretenue avec Kristen Leverone, directrice générale du département DL chez LHH. Elle a déclaré par courriel que l'incertitude économique actuelle met à l'épreuve les dirigeants (niveau C) chargés de guider leurs équipes à travers les turbulences. Leverone a souligné que, selon les résultats du sondage, 89 % des dirigeants considèrent « l'agilité et la capacité de s'adapter aux changements constants » comme un défi important, ajoutant que c'est une source de pression considérable. « Il est clair que la santé d'une entreprise, en particulier dans l'environnement actuel, est étroitement liée à l'investissement dans le personnel. Les dirigeants (niveau C) s'accordent largement à dire que la requalification des employés (76 %), le recrutement et la fidélisation (79 %) et la gestion des équipes à distance (79 %) gagneront en importance dans l'avenir du travail », a-t-elle noté. « Cependant, lors de la mise en œuvre de programmes de développement interne, les dirigeants peinent à s'assurer que les employés utilisent les ressources disponibles et consacrent du temps à leur perfectionnement professionnel. » Le rapport reconnaît que les compétences en gestion du changement et en conduite du changement ne sont pas innées. Il cite le Dr Joshua Margolis, président du programme de développement du leadership de la Harvard Business School, qui a déclaré : « Il est impératif que les dirigeants comprennent les évolutions de leur environnement afin d'assurer la pertinence et la pérennité de leurs organisations. » Leverone conseille aux clients d'investir dans la création d'une culture interne de développement où les employés peuvent s'approprier leur parcours et faire progresser leur carrière grâce à des expériences d'apprentissage qui leur fournissent les compétences spécifiques qu'ils recherchent. « Cela signifie qu'il faut dépasser les simples programmes de formation ponctuels et encourager les employés à apprendre et à s'améliorer continuellement, idéalement dans un environnement collaboratif où ils peuvent partager leurs connaissances », a-t-elle expliqué. « Cet état d'esprit devrait commencer au sommet, avec des dirigeants qui reconnaissent et célèbrent les employés qui investissent dans leur développement, encourageant les autres à faire de même. Le développement du leadership est optimal lorsqu'il s'agit d'un processus bidirectionnel et participatif qui intègre les points de vue de la prochaine génération sur les questions de diversité, d'équité et d'inclusion (DEI), de responsabilité sociale des entreprises (RSE) et de compétences. » Leverone souligne qu'il n'existe pas d'approche unique en matière de DL. Elle conclut : « Il est important de comprendre ce qui fonctionne pour votre entreprise et d'aider les clients à trouver les solutions qui répondent le mieux à leurs besoins. »

article_content: Bangkok relies on dedicated Thai council workers to prevent sewage overflow, though their task is far from glamorous. These laborers regularly descend into the city's underground drain network, which snakes beneath roads and buildings, armed with only buckets and their own hands. They manually clear the accumulated sludge and refuse to avert potential floods. The build-up in these waterways requires consistent clearing; otherwise, Bangkok faces a significant risk of inundation. The workers have no automated system to remove the waste. They must climb into the waterways and manually fill buckets with the black muck, then use basic lifting devices to haul them out. As seen in images, a council worker can be seen attaching a bucket of sludge, which he removed by hand, to a lifting device in Bangkok. Recently, these laborers entered an underground canal functioning as both a sewer and stormwater drain beneath a major road in the Thai capital. Bangkok's drainage problems have long been a challenge for residents. A particularly heavy rainfall in 2012 caused widespread flooding when rubbish and sand blocked the city's sewer system. Following that incident, the Corrections Department deployed 40 inmates to clean a seven-kilometer stretch of sewers. A worker is pictured waist-deep in muck as a bucket of waste is lifted during a cleaning operation in Bangkok. Without this regular manual cleaning, Bangkok risks the rivers of sludge overflowing during rainfall. Another image shows a council worker, smiling as he emerges from a manhole leading to an underground canal serving as a sewer under a main road.

Ces travailleurs descendent régulièrement dans le réseau de drainage souterrain de la ville, qui serpente sous les routes et les bâtiments, équipés seulement de seaux et de leurs mains. Ils retirent manuellement les boues et les déchets accumulés afin d'éviter d'éventuelles inondations. L'accumulation dans ces canaux nécessite un nettoyage constant, sinon Bangkok risque une inondation importante. Les employés ne disposent d'aucun système automatisé pour retirer les déchets. Ils doivent grimper dans les canaux et remplir manuellement des seaux de boue noire, puis utiliser des dispositifs de levage rudimentaires pour les remonter. Comme le montrent les images, on peut voir un employé municipal attacher un seau de boue, qu'il a extrait à la main, à un dispositif de levage à Bangkok. Récemment, ces travailleurs ont pénétré dans un canal souterrain servant à la fois d'égout et de drain d'eaux pluviales sous une artère principale de la capitale thaïlandaise. Les problèmes de drainage de Bangkok représentent depuis longtemps un défi pour les habitants. Des pluies particulièrement fortes en 2012 ont causé des inondations généralisées lorsque des ordures et du sable ont obstrué le réseau d'égouts de la ville. Suite à cet incident, le département des services correctionnels a déployé 40 détenus pour nettoyer une section de sept kilomètres d'égouts. Un travailleur est photographié enfoncé jusqu'à la taille dans la boue tandis qu'un seau de déchets est soulevé lors d'une opération de nettoyage à Bangkok. Sans ce nettoyage manuel régulier, Bangkok risque de voir les eaux boueuses déborder lors de fortes pluies. article_content: A young cygnet stayed close to her father as he struggled in the canal, unaware of his impending fate. He floated aimlessly, a mere shadow of his former self. The swan eventually sought refuge in the rushes, drifting between consciousness and unconsciousness, with the cygnet nestled on his back for comfort. The adult swan had to be euthanized, possibly due to contaminated bread. The mother swan was also found near death, suffering from the same suspected poisoning. Rescuers arrived but were unable to save either of the adult swans. The orphaned cygnet is now in the care of a wildlife rescue center. The RSPCA has launched an investigation into the deaths, which occurred on Sunday evening in Church, Lancashire, along the Leeds and Liverpool Canal. Passers-by noticed the swans' distress and alerted authorities after observing them in a semi-conscious state. A dog walker contacted the RSPCA. Despite being protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act, the swans could not be saved. Contaminated bread was reportedly discovered nearby, fueling suspicions of poisoning. Community leaders have expressed outrage, describing the act as 'despicable' and 'beyond belief'. An RSPCA spokeswoman confirmed that two lethargic adult swans were reported near a canal in Peel Bank, Church. The swans, along with their cygnet, were taken to a vet, where the adults were euthanized. The RSPCA is exploring poisoning as a possible cause, expressing gratitude to the dog walker who reported the incident. The dog walker recounted finding the swans surrounded by concerned individuals. He initially believed they had been physically attacked and later posted photos online seeking information about the culprits. Local councillor Peter Britcliffe condemned the act, questioning the motives of those responsible.

article_content: EU Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker has publicly criticized David Cameron's handling of EU matters, stating he was ‘not frightened’ to confront him. Juncker asserted he is ‘not the type who trembles in front of prime ministers’ and suggested Cameron faces resistance from other EU leaders. These remarks come as Cameron struggles to reduce a £1.7 billion surcharge requested by the EU, intended to offset the UK's strong economic growth while other European economies faltered. Juncker implied Cameron faces an uphill battle in persuading other EU leaders to reduce Britain's financial contributions. Cameron expressed outrage last month after the budget demand was leaked during a Brussels summit and vowed to avoid paying ‘anything like’ the demanded £1.7 billion by December 1. Angela Merkel reportedly rebuffed Cameron at a summit two weeks prior, stating the bill must be paid. Juncker stated, ‘I don't have a problem with David Cameron. He has a problem with the other prime ministers.’ To lower Britain’s contributions, Cameron must persuade France and Germany to accept a reduction in their expected rebates. The French government is slated for a £788.7 million rebate, while Germany anticipates £614 million, following a recalculation of each EU economy's performance. EU finance ministers are expected to inform George Osborne on Friday that the full surcharge is due next month. Ed Miliband criticized Cameron in the Commons regarding his handling of the EU budget negotiations. The article includes a chart comparing the UK's EU bill with those of other member states. Cameron may be offered the option to pay the surcharge in interest-free installments. Juncker cautioned, ‘I'm not frightened of any prime ministers. I am not a man who trembles before Prime Ministers or other senior figures. I accept people criticising the Commission… But I do not accept unjustified criticisms, everybody needs to know that. There will no longer be attacks on the Commission without a reaction.’ Following his first press conference as Commission president, Juncker appeared to single out Italian PM Matteo Renzi and Cameron for criticism. He informed the European Parliament that he disapproved of ‘certain prime ministers’ behavior after the additional cash demands were revealed at the European Council summit. Britain's European Commissioner Jonathan Hill held discussions with Juncker today. Juncker told Parliament, ‘I took notes and when I compared what they had said inside the room with what they said outside, they did not tally up.’ Speaking to reporters in Brussels, Juncker stated, ‘I said yesterday at the Parliament that I am not the leader of a gang of anonymous bureaucrats, I am the leader of 28 political commissioners...when anyone tries to take apart the Commission before it has even started its work, I will react.’ He reiterated, ‘I don't have a problem with Mr Renzi… I don't have a problem with Mr Cameron. Mr Cameron has a problem with the other Prime Ministers.’ Responding to Juncker's comments, Cameron's spokesman affirmed that the Prime Minister prioritizes British interests and works closely with EU counterparts. Regarding reports of potential interest-free installments for the surcharge, Cameron's spokesman emphasized the ‘unacceptability of the scale of the bill’. Osborne expressed confidence in securing a reduction, while Cameron deemed the demanded sum unacceptable – critics suggesting it punishes Britain’s economic success. Concurrently, the European Court of Auditors issued a critical report on the EU's £117 billion budget management. The ECA estimated that 3.5 to 5.9 percent of the EU budget – between £4 billion and £7 billion – was misspent. The report also criticized the 2007/13 budget process for prioritizing spending over achieving results due to a ‘use it or lose it’ approach.

article_content: The Attorney General has affirmed that Dave Lee Travis’s three-month suspended sentence for indecent assault was “neither wrong in principle nor unduly lenient” and will stand. The disgraced DJ was found guilty of molesting a researcher and received a three-month suspended sentence, a decision that was referred to the Attorney General after public criticism that it was too lenient. However, Jeremy Wright QC, the Attorney General, decided that the 69-year-old’s sentence for groping a 22-year-old TV researcher on the 'Mrs Merton Show' in 1995 would not be appealed. Dave Lee Travis was pictured speaking outside Southwark Crown Court in London in September, after being sentenced to three months in prison, suspended for two years, for indecently assaulting a TV researcher. The suspended sentence was considered for referral to the Court of Appeal after four members of the public contacted the Attorney General’s Office to complain about its perceived leniency. A spokesman for the Attorney General’s Office stated: “The Attorney General, Jeremy Wright QC MP, has decided not to refer David Griffin’s suspended prison sentence to the Court of Appeal, as he does not believe they would find it unduly lenient and increase it. “The judge acknowledged the seriousness of the offense by imposing a three-month sentence of imprisonment, the maximum under the guidelines being six months. “Suspending that sentence was neither wrong in principle nor unduly lenient.” Travis was found guilty of indecently assaulting a TV researcher who was working on the 'Mrs Merton Show' in 1995. Travis is pictured (left) on the last episode of 'Top of the Pops' in 2006 with Janice Long and Jimmy Savile, who has since been exposed as a prolific paedophile. Savile triggered the launch of Scotland Yard's Operation Yewtree. Travis, whose real name is David Griffin, was found guilty at London’s Southwark Crown Court and sentenced by Judge Anthony Leonard last month. During his trial, the jury heard that the former 'Top Of The Pops' presenter experienced a “weird sexual thrill” when he indecently assaulted the victim in 1995. She is now a successful TV personality. The trial revealed he cornered her in a BBC television studio corridor where she was smoking. The Attorney General is Jeremy Wright QC. He then commented on her “poor little lungs” before squeezing her breasts for 10 to 15 seconds. Travis, a household name in the 1970s, was found not guilty on a second indecent assault charge, and the jury was discharged after failing to reach a verdict on a count of sexual assault. He faced a retrial after jurors failed to reach verdicts on those two charges earlier this year. He was cleared of 12 counts of indecent assault at his original trial in February. The 69-year-old claimed the authorities wasted ‘millions’ on the investigation into allegations against him spanning several decades. He argued the single guilty verdict did not prove he is a ‘sexual predator’ and left him ‘mortified and disappointed’. Travis maintained his innocence throughout the trial and dismissed other women's claims of being groped by him as 'fantasists and liars'. Travis, of Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire, was first arrested in October 2012 under Operation Yewtree. Operation Yewtree was launched by Scotland Yard following allegations against the late DJ Jimmy Savile.

article_content: Japanese conglomerate SoftBank on Friday divested a 2.5% stake in PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, for Rs 871 crore through open market transactions. The sale was executed through SoftBank's affiliates, SVF India Holdings (Cayman) Ltd and SVF Python II (Cayman) Ltd. Buyers of the shares included Tata Mutual Fund, Kotak MF, Societe Generale, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore Pte, Nomura Singapore, Pioneer Investment Fund Scheme II, Saudi Central Bank, Goldman Sachs (Singapore) Pte, and Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius, among others. According to block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), SVF India Holdings (Cayman) sold 3,097,576 shares, while SVF Python II (Cayman) disposed of 8,323,635 shares, representing 0.7% and 1.8% stakes in PB Fintech, respectively. The shares were offloaded at an average price of Rs 762.80 each, bringing the total transaction value to Rs 871.21 crore. At the end of the June quarter, SVF Python II (Cayman) held a 4.39% stake in the company, according to shareholding data. Following the stake sale, shares of PB Fintech declined by 0.73%, closing at Rs 761.40 on the NSE. In December 2022, SoftBank had previously sold a 5.1% stake in Policybazaar for Rs 1,043 crore through a similar open market transaction. PB Fintech, co-founded by Yashish Dahiya and Alok Bansal in 2008, operates the online insurance platform Policybazaar and the credit comparison portal Paisabazaar. The company went public in November 2021.

article_content: In Istanbul, police established barricades around Taksim Square and used water cannons to break up crowds on Saturday, preventing protestors from entering Gezi Park, the focal point of demonstrations for over a month. Interior Minister Muammer Guler stated the government will not allow 'unauthorized' protests within the park. He clarified that while Gezi Park can be used freely, 'illegal' demonstrations and tent encampments are prohibited. Guler added that police are actively preventing unlawful gatherings throughout Istanbul. Eyewitnesses reported the use of tear gas and water cannons on Istiklal Street, a primary route to Taksim Square. An Istanbul court invalidated portions of the Taksim development plan, including the reconstruction of old barracks in Gezi Park. Following the court's decision, Taksim Solidarity, a coalition of activists and civic groups, urged people to convene in Gezi Park, which has been closed to the public since June 16. Taksim Solidarity declared their intention to personally deliver the court ruling that cancels the project aimed at altering the character of Gezi Park to those who have closed it off. They also stated their aim to reopen the park to the public. An eyewitness, Irem Koker, noted that authorities were attempting to prevent people from even reaching Istiklal Street. CNN reporters witnessed several arrests. One protestor criticized the situation as resembling 'a police state' as water cannons were deployed. Some residents voiced their frustration with the police blockades. One woman recounted being stopped at multiple entrances to Taksim, expressing concern for her waiting child and disillusionment with the police force. She also mentioned praying for the police officer but no longer does so. Amid ongoing clashes in the Beyoglu district, Istanbul Governor Huseyin Avni Mutlu addressed a viral video showing individuals armed with swords attacking pedestrians in the Talimhane area near Taksim Square. The video depicted one of the men striking a woman with the sword and kicking her. The video also showed police intervention to stop the attackers. An eyewitness reported seeking refuge in a building in Talimhane with other protesters after witnessing the sword-wielding individuals. The witness described the attackers as running and swinging 'rounded swords,' suggesting they were trying to intimidate people. Governor Mutlu stated that the suspects involved in the attacks had been apprehended. He added that a security officer was injured while attempting to detain one of the attackers. The Istanbul governor announced that Gezi Park would reopen to the public on Sunday, but reiterated that Taksim Solidarity's call for a demonstration was illegal and would not be permitted. He said that police would issue warnings to prevent any unlawful gatherings. Following more than an hour of skirmishes between police and protestors, Istiklal Street returned to calm. However, a significant police presence remained, preventing pedestrian access to Taksim Square.

Au milieu des affrontements en cours dans le quartier de Beyoglu, le gouverneur d'Istanbul, Huseyin Avni Mutlu, a réagi à une vidéo virale montrant des individus armés d'épées attaquant des piétons dans le quartier de Talimhane, près de la place Taksim. La vidéo montrait l'un des hommes frappant une femme avec une épée et lui donnant des coups de pied dans le bas du dos. La vidéo a également montré l'intervention de la police pour arrêter les agresseurs. Un témoin oculaire a déclaré s'être réfugié dans un immeuble à Talimhane avec d'autres manifestants après avoir vu les individus brandissant des épées. Le témoin a décrit les assaillants comme courant et brandissant des 'épées arrondies', suggérant qu'ils essayaient d'intimider les gens. Le gouverneur Mutlu a déclaré que les suspects impliqués dans les attaques avaient été appréhendés. Il a ajouté qu'un agent de sécurité avait été blessé en tentant d'arrêter l'un des agresseurs. Le gouverneur d'Istanbul a annoncé que le parc Gezi rouvrirait au public dimanche, mais a réaffirmé que l'appel de Taksim Solidarity à manifester était illégal et ne serait pas autorisé. Il a déclaré que la police donnerait des avertissements afin d'empêcher tout rassemblement illégal. Après plus d'une heure d'échauffourées entre la police et les manifestants, le calme est revenu sur la rue Istiklal. Cependant, une forte présence policière est restée, empêchant l'accès des piétons à la place Taksim.

article_content: After years of foreign dominance, the prospect of a French winner at the Tour de France is now a realistic possibility. The last French victory was in 1985 when Bernard Hinault secured his fifth title. He is one of only six cyclists to have won all three major tours: Italy, Spain, and France, a feat also achieved by 2014 Tour winner Vincenzo Nibali. Since Hinault's win, French success has been limited; Richard Virenque's second place in 1997 was the last time a French rider reached the podium until 2014. In 2014, Jean-Christophe Peraud and Thibaut Pinot finished approximately eight minutes behind Nibali, securing second and third place respectively, which was greatly celebrated by the success-starved French public. Further hope was provided by Romain Bardet, who competed with Pinot for the best young rider's white jersey and finished a respectable sixth. L'Equipe's headline, 'The French, promise for 2015,' reflected anticipation for the next Tour. Pinot's brief lead over Nibali on the Pyrenees' 16th stage excited fans, even though his primary objective was to gain time on Bardet for the white jersey. Peraud, despite being 37 and a road circuit professional only since 2009, leveraged his time-trialing skills to surpass Pinot. Pinot and Bardet are considered promising talents for the future. Stephen Farrand from Cyclingnews.com noted the positive impact of strong performances by home riders, increasing enthusiasm for the race and highlighting French patriotism. Thomas Voeckler's relentless spirit has been a source of patriotism for a decade. His unexpected 10-day lead in the 2004 Tour made him a national hero, amidst suspicions of Lance Armstrong's doping. With Armstrong's disgrace, cycling is perceived to have cleaned up, with no positive tests in the 2014 edition. Farrand believes the French stand to gain the most from this cleaner environment, as their historical anti-doping stance enables them to compete for the yellow jersey. The possibility of a French victory in 2015 depends on Nibali's continued performance and the return of Froome and Contador. Farrand described Nibali as a 'most deserved winner', noting his significant lead and stage wins. Nibali's victory also revitalizes Italian cycling, which has faced challenges from doping scandals and economic issues. Despite previous wins in other major tours, Nibali was initially underestimated by the media. His strategic stage win in Sheffield and strong performance on the cobbled fifth stage established his lead. Nibali secured additional stage wins in the Alps and Pyrenees, maintaining his lead over French and Spanish competitors. La Gazzetta dello Sport gave Nibali top billing, featuring a tribute from Hinault. Hinault hopes to present the yellow jersey to a French cyclist at the Champs-Elysees in coming years. Warren Barguil, considered a 'huge talent' by Hinault, and sprinters like Coquard and Bouhanni, also offer promise for French cycling. Despite Barguil's omission from his team, French sprinting talent is emerging, potentially challenging cyclists such as Kittel and Cavendish. Overall, these factors point to a potential renaissance for cycling in France.

article_content: In today's digital era, businesses are increasingly adopting digital marketing as a core strategy for connecting with their intended audience. Digital marketing provides various benefits that help businesses expand, interact with clients, and maintain a competitive edge. While it offers many advantages, it also presents challenges and drawbacks. This article explores ten key advantages and disadvantages of digital marketing and explains why it has become essential for business success. Digital marketing has transformed how businesses market products and engage with customers. Understanding both its advantages and disadvantages is vital for effective strategy development. Balancing these aspects is crucial for crafting a digital marketing strategy tailored to specific business needs. Digital marketing facilitates reaching a global audience by overcoming geographical constraints and expanding your market via internet connectivity. Compared to traditional methods like print or TV ads, digital marketing often proves more economical, offering diverse cost-effective strategies like social media advertising and email marketing. Digital marketing allows precise campaign targeting towards specific demographics, ensuring the message reaches the intended recipients efficiently. Digital marketing provides real-time analytics for tracking campaign performance, enabling data-driven decisions and strategy optimization. Digital marketing fosters two-way communication, building relationships through engagement on social media, comments, and direct messaging. Digital marketing facilitates highly personalized campaigns using customer data to deliver tailored content and offers for increased relevance and appeal. The agility in the digital landscape allows for rapid adjustments to marketing strategies, ensuring campaigns remain relevant. Digital marketing, through targeted and personalized content, leads to higher conversion rates by reaching the correct audience. An always-on online presence allows potential customers constant access to websites and social media platforms. Digital marketing enables smaller businesses to compete with larger ones via cost-effective digital strategies. The digital space's saturation can create visibility challenges, increasing advertising expenses. Frequent algorithm updates from platforms like Google and social media can impact marketing efforts. Ad-blockers may reduce the visibility of digital ads, affecting business reach. Stricter privacy regulations require complex adherence from businesses operating internationally. Managing digital marketing campaigns often requires technical skills that may be difficult to acquire. While cost-effective long-term, initial setup and quality content creation can demand significant initial investment. Short internet user attention spans require compelling content creation. Negative online feedback can spread rapidly, requiring effective brand reputation management. Digital marketing results can be unpredictable due to factors like shifting consumer behavior. Technical issues can disrupt user experiences and damage digital marketing efforts. Advantages and disadvantages of digital marketing are significant and compelling for global business reach and engagement. Embracing digital marketing is essential for modern business success. Harness digital marketing's power to propel business success, whether you’re a startup or an established brand. Recognizing potential disadvantages alongside numerous advantages is crucial for developing effective strategies that maximize benefits while mitigating downsides. Digital marketing requires informed and adaptable strategies for sustained success.

article_content: In New Delhi, Indian authorities greeted Myanmar's military junta leader on Sunday, aiming to boost diplomatic and economic relations. General Than Shwe's five-day visit includes tours of sacred Buddhist sites, meetings with Indian officials, and a visit to Mahatma Gandhi's shrine before talks with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. A 'treaty of friendship' was signed in 1951, and bilateral trade has risen to nearly $1 billion, according to Indian officials. Several Indian companies have invested in Myanmar's energy sector, and India's space agency helped set up a data center in Yangon for remote sensing. The visit follows U.S. Secretary Clinton's call for regional pressure on Myanmar to comply with UN human rights resolutions. Clinton described life in Myanmar as 'dangerous' for its inhabitants and urged democratic reforms. The general will also tour India's IT hub in Hyderabad and the industrial center in Jamshedpur; this is the second visit by a top junta administrator in a year.

Un 'traité d'amitié' a été signé en 1951, et le commerce bilatéral s'élève désormais à près d'un milliard de dollars, selon les responsables indiens. Plusieurs entreprises indiennes ont investi dans le secteur énergétique du Myanmar, et l'agence spatiale indienne a aidé à mettre en place un centre de données à Yangon pour la télédétection. Cette visite fait suite à l'appel de la secrétaire d'État américaine, Hillary Clinton, demandant une pression régionale sur le Myanmar afin qu'il respecte les résolutions de l'ONU relatives aux droits de l'homme. article_content: A recent poll indicates that Prince William enjoys greater popularity than the Queen, with a higher percentage of people holding a 'favorable' opinion of the Duke compared to his grandmother. Nevertheless, both royals are considerably more favored than prominent UK politicians, including Prime Minister David Cameron. The survey reveals that 68% of respondents have a positive view of Prince William, while 63% feel similarly about the Queen. Prince Charles trails behind his son and mother, securing a 43% approval rating; however, he still outranks any Westminster figure. Only 28% of people view Prime Minister David Cameron favorably, slightly surpassing UKIP's Nigel Farage, whose rating stands at 26%. Boris Johnson, the Mayor of London, emerges as the most popular British politician, boasting a 41% favorable view among those surveyed. In contrast, less than a fifth of respondents see Labour leader Ed Miliband in a positive light—fewer than Foreign Secretary William Hague, and on par with Chancellor George Osborne. Despite recent disagreements, Theresa May maintains more public favor at 16% than Michael Gove, whose approval rating is a mere 9%. Reflecting his party's declining poll numbers, Liberal Democrat Nick Clegg is admired by just 13% of those polled. The poll also indicates a tightening of Labour's lead over the Tories to 34% versus 32%—the narrowest gap in nearly two and a half years, according to ComRes online research. UKIP and the Liberal Democrats each lost a point, now standing at 18% and 7%, respectively. Religious freedom was identified by only 12% of voters as a core 'British value,' following Mr. Gove's pledge to promote such values in classrooms after the Trojan Horse affair. Freedom of speech topped the list of important British values at 48%, followed by respect for the rule of law, fairness, tolerance, a sense of humor, equality, politeness, political freedom, and responsibility. Aspiration—often promoted by political figures as a fundamental British value—was selected by just 3% of respondents. The ComRes poll, commissioned by the Sunday Mirror and Independent on Sunday, surveyed 2,034 British adults.

article_content: An Australian firm, GeoResonance, asserts it has discovered plane debris in the Bay of Bengal. While not explicitly stating it's the missing Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, they are encouraging official search teams to investigate. Malaysian authorities are currently evaluating the credibility of this assertion. In contrast, Australian search teams and a satellite company remain confident the plane is located in a different region. GeoResonance specializes in geophysical surveys, using its tech to find resources like oil, gas, and minerals. Their technology, initially designed to detect hidden weaponry, can pinpoint various substances, according to director David Pope. The company leverages former Soviet defense tech, now demilitarized, to analyze weak electromagnetic fields. For the MH370 search, they looked for aluminum, then other metals to create images of possible plane parts. The potential site is about 120 miles (190 kilometers) south of Bangladesh, though the exact coordinates were shared with search officials. The official search area is thousands of miles away in the southern Indian Ocean, an area previously dismissed. GeoResonance alleges its communications were ignored, prompting the public release of their findings. Initially hesitant to go public, they felt a 'moral obligation' to share the data. Following the public release, Malaysian officials engaged with GeoResonance. However, the Australian-led Joint Agency Coordination Centre dismissed the claim, reaffirming their belief MH370 is in the southern Indian Ocean.

article_content: It's large enough to store a dozen jumbo jets or over 3,500 double-decker buses, but it's more likely to hold billions of Percy Pig sweets. article_content: A second-half penalty from David Villa secured a 1-1 draw for Barcelona against Rubin Kazan in Group D of the Champions League on Wednesday. The Spanish international striker converted the penalty on the hour mark after Andres Iniesta was fouled by Lasha Salukvadze in the penalty area. Rubin Kazan had taken the lead from a penalty after half an hour, with Ecuadorian midfielder Christian Noboa scoring past Victor Valdes after Daniel Alves fouled Vitaly Kaleshin. With Lionel Messi back after recovering from an ankle injury, Barcelona pressed for a winning goal, and Messi's 71st-minute shot was blocked by goalkeeper Sergei Ryzhikov. However, Rubin Kazan nearly secured all three points late on when Nigerian striker Obafemi Martins hit the post with a close-range header. In the other Group D match, Copenhagen secured a 2-0 victory against Panathinaikos, with goals from Martin Vingaard and Dame N'Doye, putting them top of the table with six points from two matches. Barcelona are second with four points, while Panathinaikos, who played most of the second half with 10 men after Brazilian midfielder Gilberto Silva's dismissal, are bottom with two losses. In Group C, Manchester United and Rangers both secured 1-0 wins on Wednesday and lead the table with four points each. Manchester United secured a late win at the Mestalla against Valencia with a goal from Mexican international Javier Hernandez. In Glasgow, Steven Naismith scored from close range after a header from Kirk Broadfoot to defeat Bursaspor, who are bottom of the table with no points from two matches.

article_content: A Washington state jury has convicted David Pietz of second-degree murder for strangling his wife, Nicole Pietz, to death in 2006 and dumping her body in the woods. Prosecutors argued that Pietz, then 36, attempted to conceal the murder by reporting his 32-year-old wife missing. Her nude body was discovered approximately one week later. During the Monday hearing, the victim’s family members wept openly in the courtroom when the guilty verdict was announced after a day and a half of deliberations. Pietz was arrested in March 2012 by cold case detectives following a six-year investigation largely based on circumstantial evidence. Timeline: January 28, 2006: Nicole Pietz, 32, reported missing by her husband. February 6, 2006: Her nude body was found in the woods near Burien, Washington. February 12, 2006: Memorial service held for Nicole Pietz. March 2012: David Pietz arrested and charged with second-degree murder. September 12, 2013: Murder trial begins in Seattle. October 8, 2013: Defense and prosecution rest their cases. October 14, 2013: Jury reaches a guilty verdict. Prosecutor Kristen Richardson told the press that the case hinged on minor clues, including Pietz's affairs with at least four women and his wife's mouthguard, which she was wearing when her body was found in a wooded area near Burien, according to The Seattle Times. During closing arguments, Richardson argued that Pietz had grown tired of being married to Nicole due to her reluctance to engage in a more adventurous sex life and characterized him as 'cold and callous.’ Four women testified during the trial that they had sexual relations with Pietz while he was married to Nicole. One woman testified that Pietz regularly spiked his wife's drinks with ecstasy to encourage her participation in threesomes. Pietz’s defense lawyer argued that his client was wrongly accused and that the prosecution failed to establish a clear motive or present substantial evidence, such as DNA or eyewitnesses. ‘David Pietz isn’t the first guy to step out on his spouse,’ attorney David Allen told jurors. ‘Is it a motive to kill his wife? He had bad boundaries; he’s oversexed.’ The defense argued that Nicole Pietz had a history of addiction to painkillers and relapsed after eight years of sobriety, disappearing while attempting to obtain drugs. However, toxicology reports indicated only trace amounts of prescription pills in Nicole's system and no evidence of recent drug abuse. Pietz displayed minimal emotion when the verdict was announced. He faces a sentence of 10 to 18 years in prison. Family and friends of Nicole Pietz sobbed with relief. Her sister, Tonia Zurcher, yelled, 'You're going to burn in hell, Pietz,' as he was led from the courtroom. ‘I just wanted justice for my daughter, and we got it,’ said Nicole’s mother, Gael Schneider. ‘These last 7 1/2 years have been torture for us.’ Miss Schneider added, 'She'll never come back, we got justice for her, but I'll never get to hold her again,' KING5 reported. Police indicated that evidence suggested Nicole Pietz was killed at night, contradicting Pietz's claims, as she was found with her night mouth guard in place. Detectives initially considered Pietz a suspect due to his unhappiness in the marriage. Advances in technology enabled them to build a case on circumstantial evidence leading to his arrest in March 2012. Investigators noted contradictions in his statements and that he failed a lie detector test. Pietz stated he arrived home from work around midnight on January 27, 2006, briefly greeted his wife, who was already asleep, and left for work the next morning without speaking to her, according to KOMO. Pietz reported Nicole missing after she failed to arrive at a planned dinner with friends. He claimed she was going to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting and believed she relapsed into drug use. However, forensic tests indicated she was killed around midnight on January 27. She was found wearing her night mouthguard, and her wedding ring was in cleaning solution in the bathroom, which friends said she only removed at night for cleaning. Phone records allegedly showed her phone being used at her husband's workplace, and DNA evidence suggested Pietz was the last person to drive her car, which was found two weeks after her body in a parking lot near the University of Washington. Defense attorneys maintain their case is weak due to the absence of eyewitnesses.

article_content: As the NBA playoffs tip off, keep an eye on the team jerseys. Beyond the usual team names, player numbers, and surnames, there's a chance these classic designs might not be around forever. According to a New York Times report by Richard Sandomir, NBA team owners recently reviewed advertising concepts during a New York meeting. Mannequins displayed altered Chicago Bulls and Boston Celtics jerseys, each showcasing different levels of ad integration. One version swapped the team's name for a corporate sponsor, another placed the sponsor's name below the player number, and a third added the logo to the jersey strap. Currently, the NBA hasn't made a final decision about introducing ads on jerseys. None of the major North American sports associations, including MLB, NFL, and NHL, permit advertising on their uniforms. However, sports like auto racing, soccer, and golf do allow athletes to display brand endorsements on their clothing. When asked about the possibility of ads on jerseys, NBA Deputy Commissioner Adam Silver acknowledged some fans might disapprove. Yet, he emphasized the NBA's global presence and the prevalence of uniform advertising in other sports and internationally. If the NBA moves forward and becomes the first major American league to permit advertising on uniforms, initial opposition could quickly fade as people adapt. While advertising was once regarded as intrusive, it has become both widespread and a status symbol. Companies now pay to promote themselves at charity events, school stadiums, and college reunions, signifying success. The term 'selling out' has lost its negative connotation as corporate brands have effectively elevated their presence. Consumers willingly pay to wear brands like Nike, effectively promoting them for free. While those paid to wear sandwich boards get compensated, consumers pay for the privilege of brand endorsement. Resisting this trend seems futile. The Chicago Bulls won championships at both the traditionally named Chicago Stadium and the sponsored United Center, illustrating the normalization of commercialism. Similarly, Wrigley Field, named after a chewing-gum magnate, was an early example of unavoidable advertising. With the stigma around advertising in unconventional places diminished, NBA players may resist ads on jerseys until they secure a portion of the sponsorship revenue. Ultimately, profitability may trump tradition. Beyond sports, other struggling sectors like the Postal Service and the financial system could explore advertising on stamps and currency. While there would be practical considerations, such as brand conflicts on currency, the potential revenue could be significant. James Dean's plain white T-shirt, once a symbol of cool, would now be seen as a wasted advertising opportunity. Savor the unadorned jerseys during this year's playoffs. The surprising aspect isn't the consideration of ads on uniforms, but that it has taken so long for this to happen.

article_content: Bensen Johnson, the seven-year-old son of fallen Utah Sergeant Derek Johnson, held his father's badge at the state's annual law enforcement memorial in Salt Lake City. Sergeant Johnson was one of two Utah officers who died in the line of duty in the past year. Bensen and his mother, Shante Johnson, attended the memorial to honor Sergeant Johnson. The names of Sergeant Derek Johnson of Draper and Sergeant Cory Wride of Utah County were added to the Utah Law Enforcement Memorial's Honor Wall on the Capitol's west lawn. Johnson and Wride's names join those of 137 other peace officers who died in the line of duty. Both Wride and Johnson were fatally shot in their patrol cars after stopping to assist motorists. Wride was killed on January 30, and Johnson on September 1. Following Johnson's death, Timothy Troy Walker was charged with aggravated murder. Authorities stated that Walker and his former girlfriend, Traci Vaillancourt, were in the vehicle that Sgt. Johnson approached before being shot. Investigators believe Walker shot Vaillancourt in the back after shooting Johnson, then turned the gun on himself. Walker has appeared in court with a device supporting his jaw. Sergeant Derek Johnson, a father of one, was fatally shot after stopping near Walker's Volvo. Around 10,000 people attended Sergeant Derek Johnson's funeral a week after his death. Johnson is survived by his wife and son. Vaillancourt was charged with obstructing justice, but her defense maintains that she is a victim. In December, Sergeant Johnson's family donated a tree in his honor to the Utah Festival of Trees. The tree was decorated with police handcuffs, ornaments with ribbons from his funeral, and challenge coins from law enforcement agencies worldwide. The tree is now at Draper City Hall. At Sergeant Johnson's funeral, Bensen, then six, watched as nearly 10,000 people gathered at the Maverick Center outside Salt Lake City. Bensen and Shante held flags as six Draper police officers escorted Sergeant Derek Johnson's casket to the front of the arena. 'The streets of Draper City were made safer by Sgt Derek Johnson,' his family wrote in his obituary. 'Understanding the risk, he gave his life while on duty Sept 1, 2013, at the age of 32.' 'He was married to his high school sweetheart Shante Sidwell with whom he had a 6-year-old son Bensen.' 'He was the recipient of many awards and made a difference. He loved his family, hunting, running, hiking and giving service.'

Le sergent Johnson était l'un des deux policiers de l'Utah décédés dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions au cours de l'année écoulée. Bensen et sa mère, Shante Johnson, ont assisté à la cérémonie commémorative en l'honneur du sergent Johnson. Les noms du sergent Derek Johnson de Draper et du sergent Cory Wride du comté de l'Utah ont été ajoutés au mur d'honneur du mémorial des forces de l'ordre de l'Utah, sur la pelouse ouest du Capitole. Les noms de Johnson et Wride rejoignent ceux de 137 autres agents de la paix décédés dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions. Wride et Johnson ont tous deux été mortellement abattus dans leurs voitures de patrouille après s'être arrêtés pour aider des automobilistes. Wride a été tué le 30 janvier et Johnson le 1er septembre. Après la mort de Johnson, Timothy Troy Walker a été accusé de meurtre avec circonstances aggravantes. Les autorités ont déclaré que Walker et son ancienne petite amie, Traci Vaillancourt, se trouvaient dans le véhicule que le sergent Johnson a approché avant d'être abattu. Les enquêteurs pensent que Walker a tiré sur Vaillancourt dans le dos après avoir tiré sur Johnson, puis a retourné l'arme contre lui-même. Walker a comparu devant le tribunal avec un dispositif soutenant sa mâchoire. Le sergent Derek Johnson, père d'un enfant, a été mortellement abattu après s'être arrêté près de la Volvo de Walker. Environ 10 000 personnes ont assisté aux funérailles du sergent Derek Johnson une semaine après sa mort. Johnson laisse dans le deuil sa femme et son fils. Vaillancourt a été accusée d'entrave à la justice, mais sa défense maintient qu'elle est une victime. En décembre, la famille du sergent Johnson a fait don d'un arbre en son honneur au Festival des arbres de l'Utah. L'arbre était décoré de menottes de police, de décorations avec des rubans de ses funérailles et de pièces de défi des forces de l'ordre du monde entier. L'arbre se trouve maintenant à l'hôtel de ville de Draper. Aux funérailles du sergent Johnson, Bensen, alors âgé de six ans, a regardé près de 10 000 personnes se rassembler au Maverick Center, à l'extérieur de Salt Lake City. Bensen et Shante ont brandi des drapeaux pendant que six policiers de Draper escortaient le cercueil du sergent Derek Johnson jusqu'à l'avant de l'arène. 'Les rues de Draper City ont été rendues plus sûres par le sergent Derek Johnson', a écrit sa famille dans sa notice nécrologique. 'Conscient du risque, il a donné sa vie alors qu'il était en service le 1er septembre 2013, à l'âge de 32 ans.' 'Il était marié à Shante Sidwell, son amour de lycée, avec qui il a eu un fils de 6 ans, Bensen.' 'Il a reçu de nombreux prix et a fait une différence. Il aimait sa famille, la chasse, la course à pied, la randonnée et le service.'

article_content: Indianapolis police are searching for the mother of a newborn daughter whose body was found in a wooded area of Eagle Creek Park. The baby was wrapped in a college sweatshirt. Officers were alerted to the discovery on Sunday afternoon after a hiker found the baby in the park, located on the outskirts of Indianapolis. Investigators believe the baby was approximately one day old, with the umbilical cord still attached. The discovery was made roughly 30 yards from a parking area on the park's northwest side, concealed under a branch. The deceased newborn was found swaddled in a blue sweatshirt displaying the logo of Aviation Maintenance Vincennes University-Indianapolis. Emergency responders pronounced the baby dead at the scene, on the northern edge of the 3,900-acre park, around 4:30 p.m. According to police, the newborn was found wrapped in the mentioned blue sweatshirt. Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department spokesman Christopher Wilburn stated that forensics investigators are using the sweatshirt to try to identify and locate the mother. 'We want to do what we can. It's very tragic. There may be some DNA on that sweatshirt,' Wilburn told The Indy Channel. The coroner indicated that it is currently unknown whether the baby was born alive or stillborn, and the gestational age remains undetermined. Further tests will be conducted to ascertain the cause and manner of death. Officials emphasize that alternatives were available to the mother instead of abandoning the baby. Indiana's Safe Haven Infant Protection Act, enacted in 2000, allows individuals to anonymously surrender an unwanted infant without fear of legal repercussions, according to WISH-TV. Under the Safe Haven law, a parent, family member, friend, minister, social worker, or any responsible adult can relinquish custody of a baby less than 30 days old at a hospital emergency room, fire station, or police station in Indiana, provided the child shows no signs of abuse. Authorities are asking anyone who recognizes the blue college sweatshirt or has information regarding the mother's whereabouts to contact (317) 327-3475. Individuals wishing to remain anonymous can contact Crime Stoppers at 262-TIPS (8477).

article_content: When a hungry mother-of-two took a bite from a chicken, bacon, and lettuce sandwich from Tesco, she encountered an unexpected surprise. Katie Crabtree was shocked to discover what appeared to be a rodent inside the pre-packaged snack she had purchased from a Tesco branch in Stockport. The horrified 31-year-old noticed the ‘furry object’ only after partially consuming it, initially mistaking it for a piece of burnt bacon. Ms. Crabtree stated, 'I took a bite and saw this big black thing in it, but I thought it was just burnt bacon, so I swallowed it.' 'Then I realized there was something horrible in the sandwich. It was black, had hair, and I could even see a little paw. It was truly horrendous.' Ms. Crabtree said the discovery made her feel sick and stated, 'I can’t eat another packaged sandwich because I just think of that horrible thing.' She claimed that the supermarket giant attempted to ignore her after she followed up on her initial complaint with the store and head office. 'I followed up several times with the store and head office, but nobody seemed to know what was happening,' she said. 'In the end, they offered me a £10 voucher. I think they’ve fobbed me off. They need to investigate what happened to this sandwich in case further action is needed at the production site.' The supermarket chain has since apologized and provided her with a £10 voucher. Tesco issued an apology letter and stated they would investigate the matter, in addition to offering £10 as compensation. A Tesco spokesman said, 'We take any case of this nature very seriously. Sadly, on this occasion, our food safety procedures did not perform as expected. We have apologized to our customer and are urgently investigating the matter with our supplier.' In Peru, guinea pigs are a popular culinary item. The rodents are killed, skinned, and roasted on a spit. Once cooked, street vendors often arrange them in decorative poses, using vegetables to mimic tongues and eyeballs. Guinea pig has been a significant part of the Andean diet for thousands of years and remains a common dish in numerous South American countries. In Cusco, Peru, a well-known guinea pig dish is called chiriuchu, which translates to 'cold food' in Quechua, the language of the Incas. It consists primarily of guinea pig (locally known as 'cuy') alongside chicken, dried salt-beef, blood sausage, seaweed, toasted maize, cheese, fish eggs, hot pepper, and a potato and herb tortilla. Chiriuchu is frequently served during local festivals, particularly Corpus Christi, and sold from street-side stands. Its popularity has led locals to appeal to UNESCO for its recognition as part of Cusqueñan cultural heritage.

Sa popularité a conduit les habitants à demander à l'UNESCO de le reconnaître comme faisant partie du patrimoine culturel de Cusqueña.

article_content: Washington – A Senate vote on Thursday rejected nearly $5 billion intended to resolve a long-standing agreement between the Agriculture Department and minority farmers, sparking immediate recriminations and anger, particularly among African American farmers. John Boyd, the National Black Farmers Association's founder and president, voiced profound disappointment, stating, 'We're unfortunately ensnared in a larger political battle within the Senate, characterized by intense partisan division.' He added, 'It appears black farmers are consistently left behind as important legislation moves forward in the Senate,' and urged President Barack Obama to intervene. The Pigford v. Glickman case, initiated in 1997 against the U.S. Agriculture Department, was settled out of court 11 years prior. The terms set by a federal judge in 1999 stipulated that eligible farmers could each receive $50,000 to address claims of racial discrimination. Earlier, in July, the House of Representatives approved a military spending bill that incorporated funding for this settlement. However, the Senate's attempt to approve the funding failed when Republicans opposed a unanimous consent agreement proposed by Democrats, citing concerns about the Democrats' proposed payment method. According to Boyd, this was the seventh unsuccessful attempt in recent weeks to secure Senate approval for the settlement funds. Despite public endorsements from prominent members of both parties, the settlement remains unresolved. 'Everyone publicly claims to support black farmers,' Boyd noted, 'yet they can't overcome their political disputes to allow these farmers to move forward with their lives.' Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid criticized Republicans for the impasse, declaring, 'Delivering justice to those who have suffered injustice should be a bipartisan imperative.' He added in a statement, 'Republicans are treating it as a partisan issue. If they cannot set aside their obstructionist tactics to resolve this straightforward, bipartisan matter, what can we expect them to agree on with Democrats?' Boyd, however, refrained from solely blaming Republicans, stating, 'I believe both parties share responsibility for this situation.'

Il a ajouté : 'Il semble que les agriculteurs noirs soient systématiquement laissés de côté lorsque des projets de loi importants progressent au Sénat', et a exhorté le président Barack Obama à intervenir. Les conditions, fixées par un juge fédéral en 1999, stipulaient que les agriculteurs admissibles pouvaient recevoir 50 000 dollars chacun en compensation des préjudices liés à la discrimination raciale. Plus tôt, en juillet, la Chambre des représentants avait approuvé un projet de loi de finances concernant les dépenses militaires, qui incluait le financement de cet accord. Cependant, la tentative du Sénat d'approuver ce financement a échoué lorsque les républicains se sont opposés à une motion de consentement unanime proposée par les démocrates, invoquant des inquiétudes quant à la méthode de financement proposée par ces derniers. Selon M. Boyd, il s'agissait de la septième tentative infructueuse au cours des dernières semaines pour obtenir l'aval du Sénat concernant les fonds destinés au règlement. Malgré les déclarations publiques de soutien de membres éminents des deux partis, le problème n'est toujours pas résolu. 'Tout le monde affirme publiquement soutenir les agriculteurs noirs', a souligné M. Boyd, 'mais ils sont incapables de mettre de côté leurs querelles politiques pour permettre à ces agriculteurs de progresser dans leur vie.' article_content: Australian batsman Phil Hughes passed away at the age of 25, two days after being struck on the head by a bouncer. Nasser Hussain commented that cricket will reassess safety measures following Hughes' death, and while changes may occur, the sport will continue. David Lloyd described the accident as tragic and expressed sympathy for Sean Abbott. Paul Newman authored Hughes' obituary. The second one-day international between England and Sri Lanka proceeded as scheduled on Saturday. Both teams observed a two-minute silence and wore black armbands at the Premadasa Stadium in Colombo to honor Hughes. In contrast, the second day of the Pakistan-New Zealand Test in Sharjah was suspended as a mark of respect. India also cancelled their two-day warm-up game in Adelaide. The Blind World Cup game between England and Pakistan in South Africa was postponed; the tournament was scheduled to resume on Friday. Pakistan Cricket Board chairman Shaharyar Khan conveyed condolences to Hughes' family and Cricket Australia. Team manager Moin Khan shared that the entire Pakistan team was saddened and shocked by Hughes' death. New Zealand coach Mike Hesson stated that the focus was on Hughes, not cricket, and expressed devastation on behalf of the Black Caps players and management. The scoreboard at the Sharjah cricket ground displayed a message mourning Hughes' untimely demise. Pakistan leads the three-match series against New Zealand following a victory in Abu Dhabi and a draw in Dubai.

article_content: Aaron De Silva, a 21-year-old, received a life sentence with a minimum of 32 years in prison for the murder of 73-year-old Joseph Griffiths. The sentencing followed a trial at the Old Bailey. De Silva broke into Griffiths' £1.5 million residence in Fulham, South London, while armed with a knife. The victim and his wife were asleep at the time of the incident. Mr. Griffiths was discovered by his wife and a visiting friend, lying in a pool of blood, having been stabbed 22 times in the chest and abdomen after confronting De Silva in the hallway of his home. Following the gruesome act, CCTV footage showed De Silva returning to his Earls Court hostel. According to Prosecutor Brendan Finucane QC, he appeared 'cool, calm, and collected' as he washed his clothes and disposed of evidence before being apprehended three days later. Mark Griffiths, the victim's eldest son, stated that the family and friends felt a 'great sense of relief' after the verdict. He also expressed gratitude toward the police and commended the British legal system. Detective Inspector Simon Pickford described De Silva as an 'extremely violent individual'. The court also learned that De Silva had a history of 31 previous convictions for crimes such as robbery, burglary and carrying a knife, starting from the age of 12. In a statement read in court, Mark Griffiths conveyed that the 'senseless' murder of his father had created a significant void in their family and in the lives of all who knew him.

La victime et sa femme dormaient au moment des faits. article_content: King Charles III and Queen Camilla are currently on a four-day state visit to Kenya. During this visit, King Charles is expected to address the 'painful aspects' of the United Kingdom's colonial past. In the 1950s, over 10,000 individuals lost their lives, and numerous others were subjected to torture during the suppression of the Mau Mau revolt, a particularly violent episode in British Empire history. In 2013, the UK government conveyed its regret and provided £20 million (equivalent to $24 million) in compensation to more than 5,000 individuals; however, some feel this was insufficient. One such individual is Agnes Muthoni, aged 90. Despite her stooped posture, she steadily guides visitors to her husband's gravesite in Shamata, located in central Kenya. She diligently removes weeds growing near the grave of Elijah Kinyua, who passed away two years prior at the age of 93. Also known as General Bahati, he, like his wife, was a combatant in the 1950s uprising against British colonial authority. Muthoni held the rank of major within the Kenya Land and Freedom Army, more widely recognized as the Mau Mau. Muthoni's face lights up as she proudly displays her wedding ring, recalling that she and Elijah met after his release from detention following the revolt. He expressed a desire to marry a female fighter who had survived, believing she would understand his experiences and not label him a 'Mau Mau.' Their shared struggle brought them together. Even after Kenya achieved independence from British colonial rule, the couple, like many former Mau Mau fighters, lived discreetly. The resistance group remained officially outlawed, having been designated a terrorist organization by the colonial government, a ban that subsequent independent Kenyan administrations did not reverse. Kenyan lawyer and politician Paul Muite explains that 'three Mau Mau members could not meet; it was an offense,' labeling it 'atrocious.' The law was not changed until 2003, when Mau Mau members were finally acknowledged as freedom fighters. This delay meant that later generations were largely unaware of the historical context. Historian Caroline Elkins, who interviewed people in the 1990s, observed that many children and grandchildren were ignorant of the roots of the country's suffering that led to independence. These observations resonate today in Nairobi, where many young people have limited knowledge of the detentions and torture inflicted upon the Mau Mau, focusing more on economic issues and the potential impact of King Charles's visit.

article_content: By Ashley Collman Published: 10:44 EST, July 30, 2013 | Updated: 11:08 EST, July 30, 2013 Experts believe that a free yearly lung cancer screening could save as many as 20,000 lives. The decision was made by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF), which is comprised of 16 healthcare experts who make recommendations about preventive services. The task force gave the preventive service a 'B' rating, meaning that under the 2010 Affordable Care Act, qualified Medicare and private insurance patients could receive the annual screening free of charge. Currently, the grade is a draft recommendation and is open for public comment until August 26. After that, it will take three to six months for the final recommendation to be instituted by healthcare providers. Lifesaver: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force announced that they are recommending free lung cancer screenings for those at the highest risk of contracting the disease. Lung cancer is the deadliest cancer, killing about 160,000 people a year, because symptoms usually don't appear until it's too late. Screenings for the disease are rare because, until recently, healthcare professionals weren't sure if a CT scan could accurately find the cancer early enough to make a difference. However, recent studies show that early screening can, and does, save lives. In 2010, the National Cancer Institute held a large-scale trial involving 53,000 patients using a CT scan that detected smaller tumors. They found that the screening could reduce the lung cancer mortality rate by 16 percent among those at the highest risk of getting lung cancer. Dr. Claudia Henschke of the Mount Sinai Medical Center in New York was part of a study that advocated for early screenings. She says this decision is going to make a big difference in how many people die from the disease. Game changer: The task force estimates that as many as 20,000 of the 160,000 people diagnosed with lung cancer every year could be saved with early detection. 'Back in 1999 when we published our results, we were very confident that it was going to make a big difference,' Dr. Henschke told NBC News. 'Now, finally, it will be made available to those people who are at highest risk. I am thrilled.' These findings were used as evidence in the task force's recommendation on Monday. Nine million current and former smokers will be eligible for the yearly screening. Senior citizens are a priority, with current smokers aged 55 to 80 eligible for the procedure. Former heavy smokers who quit less than 15 years ago, those who smoked a pack a day for 30 years, and patients who smoked three packs a day for 10 years also fall into the eligible group. Task leader Dr. Michael LeFevre told Fox News that the yearly screenings can save 'a substantial number of lung cancer deaths,' estimating 20,000 of the 160,000 that happen each year in the U.S. Some are afraid this will only encourage current smokers to continue smoking if they're eligible for a free screening. However, the lung cancer test is not enough to make current smokers quit. The yearly screening involves a CT scan. If a spot shows up on the scan it could mean cancer, but it could also be emphysema, an infection, or nothing. Risky: The screenings save lives but also involve a lung biopsy to confirm the cancer, which can collapse the lung and cause death as well. Doctors must perform a lung biopsy to confirm the cancer. This involves inserting a needle into the chest and lungs to retrieve a sample. The procedure is both painful and risky and can cause the lung to collapse. A study at the National Lung Screening Trial found that for every five to six lives saved by the screening, one person died from procedures done in the screening, including collapsed lungs caused by biopsies. Dr. Harold E. Varmus, the director of the National Cancer Institute, told the New York Times that the recommendation should not 'change the way people think about lung cancer.' 'The main message is unchanged,' he said. 'Don't smoke.'
