La décision a été prise par le Groupe d'étude des services de prévention des États-Unis (USPSTF), composé de 16 experts de la santé qui émettent des recommandations sur les services de prévention. Le groupe d'étude a attribué la note « B » au service de prévention, ce qui signifie qu'en vertu de la loi de 2010 sur les soins abordables, les patients admissibles à Medicare et aux assurances privées pourraient bénéficier d'un dépistage annuel gratuit. Actuellement, cette recommandation est à l'état de projet et ouverte aux commentaires du public jusqu'au 26 août. Passé ce délai, il faudra attendre de trois à six mois pour que la recommandation finale soit mise en œuvre par les professionnels de santé. Solution vitale : Le Groupe d'étude des services de prévention des États-Unis a annoncé recommander des dépistages gratuits du cancer du poumon pour les personnes présentant le risque le plus élevé de contracter la maladie. Le cancer du poumon est le cancer le plus meurtrier, tuant environ 160 000 personnes chaque année, car les symptômes n'apparaissent généralement que lorsqu'il est trop tard. Les dépistages de cette maladie sont rares car, jusqu'à récemment, les professionnels de la santé n'étaient pas certains qu'un scanner pouvait détecter le cancer avec suffisamment de précision et à un stade précoce pour faire une différence. Cependant, des études récentes montrent qu'un dépistage précoce peut sauver des vies, et c'est le cas. En 2010, l'Institut national du cancer a mené un essai à grande échelle auprès de 53 000 patients, utilisant un scanner capable de détecter des tumeurs plus petites. Ils ont constaté que le dépistage pouvait réduire le taux de mortalité due au cancer du poumon de 16 % chez les personnes présentant le risque le plus élevé de développer un cancer du poumon. Le Dr Claudia Henschke, du centre médical Mount Sinaï de New York, a participé à une étude qui préconisait des dépistages précoces. Elle affirme que cette décision aura un impact important sur le nombre de décès dus à cette maladie. Révolution : Le groupe d'étude estime que jusqu'à 20 000 des 160 000 personnes diagnostiquées chaque année avec un cancer du poumon pourraient être sauvées grâce à une détection précoce. « En 1999, lorsque nous avons publié nos résultats, nous étions très confiants que cela ferait une grande différence », a déclaré le Dr Henschke à NBC News. « Maintenant, enfin, ce sera mis à la disposition des personnes les plus à risque. Je suis ravie. » Ces résultats ont servi de preuve pour étayer la recommandation du groupe d'étude lundi. Neuf millions de fumeurs et d'anciens fumeurs seront admissibles au dépistage annuel. Les personnes âgées sont prioritaires, les fumeurs actuels âgés de 55 à 80 ans étant admissibles à la procédure. Les anciens gros fumeurs ayant arrêté de fumer il y a moins de 15 ans, ceux qui ont fumé un paquet par jour pendant 30 ans et les patients ayant fumé trois paquets par jour pendant 10 ans font également partie du groupe admissible. Le chef du groupe d'étude, le Dr Michael LeFevre, a déclaré à Fox News que les dépistages annuels pouvaient sauver « un nombre considérable de vies emportées par le cancer du poumon », estimant ce nombre à 20 000 sur les 160 000 décès annuels aux États-Unis. Certains craignent que cela n'encourage les fumeurs actuels à continuer de fumer s'ils sont admissibles à un dépistage gratuit. Cependant, le test de dépistage du cancer du poumon n'est pas suffisant pour inciter les fumeurs actuels à arrêter de fumer. Le dépistage annuel comprend un scanner. Si une anomalie est détectée sur le scanner, cela pourrait indiquer un cancer, mais aussi de l'emphysème, une infection ou rien du tout. Risque : Les dépistages sauvent des vies, mais impliquent également une biopsie pulmonaire pour confirmer le cancer, ce qui peut entraîner un affaissement pulmonaire, voire la mort. Les médecins doivent effectuer une biopsie pulmonaire pour confirmer le diagnostic de cancer. Cela implique d'insérer une aiguille dans la poitrine et les poumons pour prélever un échantillon. La procédure est à la fois douloureuse et risquée et peut provoquer un affaissement pulmonaire. Une étude du National Lung Screening Trial a révélé que pour cinq à six vies sauvées grâce au dépistage, une personne décédait des suites d'interventions pratiquées lors du dépistage, notamment des affaissements pulmonaires causés par les biopsies. Le Dr Harold E. Varmus, directeur de l'Institut national du cancer, a déclaré au New York Times que cette recommandation ne devrait pas « changer la façon dont les gens envisagent le cancer du poumon ». « Le message principal reste inchangé », a-t-il déclaré. « Ne fumez pas. »

article_content: Nearly two years after an Air France plane vanished, resulting in the deaths of 228 people, the majority of the wreckage has been located with human remains aboard, French officials announced Monday. French Ecology and Transportation Minister Nathalie Kosciusko-Morizet stated at a press conference that the remains will be brought to the surface for identification. Submarines involved in the search discovered two engines, the fuselage, and landing gear over the weekend, according to officials. However, the flight data recorders have not been found, leaving investigators still unsure about the cause of the crash, which occurred in stormy weather on June 1, 2009. 'It's still a jigsaw puzzle,' said Alain Bouillard, who is overseeing the recovery operation. 'We do not know the location of the recorders.' Kosciusko-Morizet expressed optimism that the flight data recorder, also known as the black box, will be recovered. 'The discovery of numerous aircraft parts in a concentrated area provides hope for locating the black boxes, but we cannot be certain,' she said. The exact number of bodies remaining in the wreckage is unknown, Bouillard added. Fifty bodies were previously recovered, leaving 178 victims still missing. He declined to comment on the condition of the bodies, deeming it 'inappropriate'. The debris field spans approximately 600 meters by 200 meters (1,960 feet by 650 feet), according to officials. All recovered wreckage will be transported to France for analysis, stated Jean-Paul Troadec, head of the French air accident investigation agency, the Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses (BEA). 'Our primary goal is to determine the cause of this accident to prevent future occurrences,' he said. Three companies have until Thursday afternoon to submit proposals for raising the wreckage, he added. The recovery operation is expected to last three to four weeks and will be funded by the French government at an estimated cost of 5 million euros ($7.1 million). Authorities are withholding the precise location of the wreckage to protect the site, officials confirmed. The head of Air France described the discovery as 'positive news, offering hope that information about the accident's causes, which remain unresolved, will be found.' Air France's Pierre-Henri Gourgeon also thanked the French authorities 'for utilizing unprecedented resources to continue the search.' Investigators revealed on Sunday that they had located pieces of the Airbus A330-200, which disappeared en route from Rio de Janeiro to Paris. Following three unsuccessful searches, investigators located the wreckage using 'a revised calculation based on ocean currents and potential events,' Troadec, the BEA chief, explained on Monday. The BEA reported on Sunday that a team led by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution made the discoveries during an underwater search conducted within the past 24 hours. Analysis of debris and bodies recovered after the crash led the BEA to conclude that the plane impacted the water belly first, largely intact. Oxygen masks were not deployed, suggesting that the cabin did not depressurize, according to a 2009 BEA report. Automated messages transmitted from the plane in the minutes before the crash indicated issues with airspeed measurement, investigators stated, although they emphasized that this alone was not sufficient to cause the disaster. The crash site is situated far out in the Atlantic, requiring two to four days of travel for ships from the nearest ports in Brazil or Senegal in West Africa. The underwater terrain is characterized by underwater mountains and valleys, according to the BEA.

'C'est toujours un puzzle', a déclaré Alain Bouillard, qui supervise l'opération de récupération. 'Nous ne connaissons pas l'emplacement des enregistreurs.' Kosciusko-Morizet a exprimé son optimisme quant à la récupération de l'enregistreur de données de vol, également connu sous le nom de boîte noire. 'La découverte de nombreuses pièces d'avion dans une zone concentrée donne l'espoir de localiser les boîtes noires, mais nous ne pouvons pas en être certains', a-t-elle déclaré. Le nombre exact de corps restant dans l'épave est inconnu, a ajouté Bouillard. Cinquante corps avaient été précédemment récupérés, laissant 178 victimes toujours portées disparues. Il a refusé de commenter l'état des corps, jugeant cela 'inapproprié'. Le champ de débris s'étend sur environ 600 mètres sur 200 mètres (1 960 pieds sur 650 pieds), selon des responsables. Toutes les épaves récupérées seront transportées en France pour analyse, a déclaré Jean-Paul Troadec, chef du Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses (BEA), l'agence française d'enquête sur les accidents aériens. 'Notre objectif principal est de déterminer la cause de cet accident afin de prévenir de futurs incidents', a-t-il déclaré. Trois sociétés ont jusqu'à jeudi après-midi pour soumettre des propositions pour remonter l'épave, a-t-il ajouté. L'opération de récupération devrait durer de trois à quatre semaines et sera financée par le gouvernement français pour un coût estimé à 5 millions d'euros (7,1 millions de dollars). Les autorités gardent secrète la localisation précise de l'épave afin de protéger le site, ont confirmé des responsables. Le directeur d'Air France a décrit la découverte comme une 'nouvelle positive, offrant l'espoir que des informations sur les causes de l'accident, qui restent non résolues, seront trouvées'. Pierre-Henri Gourgeon d'Air France a également remercié les autorités françaises 'pour avoir utilisé des ressources sans précédent pour poursuivre les recherches'. Les enquêteurs ont révélé dimanche qu'ils avaient localisé des pièces de l'Airbus A330-200, qui avait disparu alors qu'il effectuait la liaison Rio de Janeiro-Paris. Après trois recherches infructueuses, les enquêteurs ont localisé l'épave en utilisant 'un calcul révisé basé sur les courants océaniques et les événements potentiels', a expliqué lundi Troadec, le chef du BEA. Le BEA a rapporté dimanche qu'une équipe dirigée par la Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution avait fait les découvertes lors d'une opération de recherche sous-marine menée au cours des dernières 24 heures. L'analyse des débris et des corps récupérés après l'accident a conduit le BEA à conclure que l'avion a impacté l'eau le ventre en premier, en grande partie intact. Les masques à oxygène n'ont pas été déployés, ce qui suggère que la cabine ne s'est pas dépressurisée, selon un rapport du BEA de 2009. Les messages automatisés transmis par l'avion dans les minutes précédant l'accident ont indiqué des problèmes de mesure de la vitesse de l'air, ont déclaré les enquêteurs, tout en soulignant que cela seul n'était pas suffisant pour provoquer la catastrophe. Le site de l'accident est situé loin dans l'Atlantique, nécessitant deux à quatre jours de voyage pour les navires depuis les ports les plus proches du Brésil ou du Sénégal en Afrique de l'Ouest. Le terrain sous-marin est caractérisé par des montagnes et des vallées sous-marines, selon le BEA.

article_content: Two days after Carlesha Freeland-Gaither's abduction in Philadelphia was captured on video, police reported a lead: her bank card was used in Maryland on Tuesday morning. According to Philadelphia Police Chief Inspector Dennis Wilson, a man used Freeland-Gaither's ATM card at 6:01 a.m. at a bank in Aberdeen, Maryland, approximately 75 miles southwest of the Philadelphia street where she was abducted on Sunday night. Wilson did not specify how the card was used or if cash was withdrawn but mentioned that surveillance video showed a man 'similar' to the person believed to have abducted the 22-year-old on Sunday night. This lead was announced shortly before Freeland-Gaither's family appealed publicly for her return. Her grandmother, Ana Mulero, stated at a news conference with Wilson in Philadelphia, 'Please return her. We just want Carlesha returned to us safely. Just return her to us. We're her family. She has a family here. We need her.' Police have not yet released the bank video. However, authorities previously released a video that depicts Freeland-Gaither being accosted by an unidentified man in Philadelphia's Germantown-Penn Knox area around 9:40 p.m. on Sunday. The video, released on Monday, shows a man approaching a woman near an intersection, then grabbing her and dragging her down the street towards the camera. The footage lacks audio, but a witness reported that Freeland-Gaither shouted for help, according to police. The video also shows Freeland-Gaither struggling with her abductor and being forced into a four-door vehicle, possibly a gray Ford Taurus. Her glasses and cell phone were dropped on the road during the struggle. Just before the vehicle drove away, Freeland-Gaither broke one of the passenger side windows, police said. Police described the abductor as a Black man of medium-heavy build, estimated to be between 25 and 30 years old. He was seen in the video wearing a dark hooded jacket, a dark hat, and dark pants. Freeland-Gaither's family told CNN affiliate WPVI that she worked as a nurse and was only a few blocks from her home when she was abducted. Investigators are uncertain whether she knew her abductor; the Philadelphia surveillance video shows no indication that she did, Wilson stated. Police have not publicly disclosed a possible motive. Authorities initially indicated that the abductor's car had a Pennsylvania license plate, but Wilson stated on Tuesday that investigators are exploring whether a Maryland plate was on the car's front. The plate is not clearly visible in the video, and police said no witness provided a plate number. Mulero mentioned that her granddaughter lived with her in Maryland for four years before returning to Philadelphia to be with other relatives and pursue her career. Officials are offering rewards totaling $42,000 for information leading to the resolution of the case, including $25,000 from the FBI, which is assisting in the investigation, Wilson said. CNN's Dana Ford contributed to this report.

article_content: A ten-year-old German boy has discovered what appears to be an Egyptian mummy inside a wooden chest in his grandmother's attic. Alexander Kettler made the find in Diepholz, northern Germany, locating the 'mummy' within a sarcophagus in a dimly lit corner of the attic, where it had remained undisturbed for at least four decades. The boy's father, Lutz Wolfgang Kettler, plans to transport the hieroglyphic-covered box to Berlin for expert authentication. In addition to the 'mummy', the chest also contained a death mask and a canopic jar, which ancient Egyptians used for storing removed organs. Mr. Kettler suspects the sarcophagus and jar are replicas but believes the mummy could be genuine. He stated, 'You just don't get the feeling that's something you could buy at a shop around the corner.' Mr. Kettler's father journeyed to North Africa in the 1950s, subsequently shipping a mysterious chest back to Germany. He mentioned that his father never discussed the chest or its contents but told the local newspaper Die Kreiszeitung that a market for genuine mummies still existed during his father's travels, which concluded over a decade ago. Mr. Kettler added that mummy 'unwrapping parties'—where authentic mummies were unwrapped, and associated trinkets distributed to guests—were once common in Germany. Dentist Mr. Kettler believes X-raying the mummy is the only way to verify its authenticity. The mummification process dates back to 3,500 BC, with the oldest known intact Egyptian mummy originating from approximately 100 years later. This mummy, identified as ID #32751, is housed at the British Museum and was apparently preserved through direct contact with the dry desert sand, although the intentionality of the mummification is unclear. Ancient Egyptians firmly believed in the afterlife and mummified both humans and animals. They believed that for one to reach the afterlife, the body needed to be recognizable, allowing the deceased to reclaim it. The chief embalmer, a priest wearing the mask of Anubis, the jackal-headed God of the dead, would first extract the brains through the nose using a hook. Then, the internal organs—lungs, stomach, intestines, and liver—were removed and placed in jars; the heart was left in place. The body's interior was rinsed with wine and spices before being covered in salt for 70 days. After 40 days, it was stuffed with linen to restore a more lifelike shape. At 70 days, it was wrapped in bandages and placed in a brightly painted coffin. Mummification was primarily reserved for the wealthy due to its cost, whereas poorer individuals could not afford it. Animals were also sometimes mummified as offerings to the Gods or to accompany their owners in the afterlife.

article_content: In the words of African-American poet Maya Angelou: 'Africa is a historical truth ... no one can know where they're going unless they know exactly where they've been and exactly how they arrived at their present place.' This quest for historical truth draws numerous visitors to Cape Coast, Ghana, a scenic coastal town boasting a stunning blue sea, tranquil beaches, and colorful fishing boats. Rather than leisurely days under the sun, these visitors seek insight into their ancestral past—the agonizing experiences of their African ancestors who were sold into slavery. Roots tourism is attracting a growing number of people of African descent, including Monique Ross and Jacques Wallace, to this once-sleepy fishing port. Ross, Wallace, and their tour group from New York explore Cape Coast Castle, a coastal fortress that once served as slave dungeons, to understand the suffering endured by their ancestors before being transported across the Atlantic. 'I'm slightly numb, actually,' Wallace confessed. 'I wasn't prepared for the stories about the way people were treated here. The tunnel, and the image of everyone bound and led down it, is tragic and overwhelming.' Ross echoed his sentiment: 'It's initially devastating. But it's important to understand the history and connect your historical past with the present.' U.S. President Barack Obama and his family visited Cape Coast Castle during their trip to Ghana in July 2009. This was a deeply emotional experience, particularly for First Lady Michelle Obama and her mother, who are descendants of slaves from South Carolina. The crumbling colonial buildings serve as a reminder that Cape Coast was once a European colonial capital, passing between the control of the Portuguese, Dutch, Swedish, Danish, and British over centuries. It thrived as the largest slave-trading outpost in West Africa, driven by the demand for slaves from European plantations in the Americas starting in the 1500s, which overshadowed the gold trade. For over three centuries, millions of captured Africans—men, women, and children—were brought from across the continent and treated like livestock on ships bound for the United States, South America, and the Caribbean. Kwesi Essel Blankson, a senior educator at Cape Coast Castle who guided Obama and his family, described the appalling conditions the slaves faced in the fortress. They were confined to cramped spaces with minimal food, water, and air, forced to live and defecate side by side, often for months. Female captives were subjected to rape and sexual abuse by guards and officials. Those who survived these conditions were forced through the 'Door of No Return,' an arched gateway with heavy doors that closed behind them before they were forced onto slave ships. 'For many, this door represents a journey from the known to the unknown,' Blankson explained. 'And from this point, resistance was anticipated.' While many tourists use Cape Coast as a base for visiting other Ghanaian attractions like Kakum National Park, the city hopes to increase roots tourism, focusing on the castle, to encourage longer stays and greater spending. This dark chapter of history tells a story not only of suffering but also of survival. Blankson noted that Obama was 'surprised, shocked, and sad, but also motivated ... because if blacks survived this, it demonstrates the resilience of human beings and a strong survival instinct.'

Cette quête de vérité historique attire de nombreux visiteurs à Cape Coast, au Ghana, une ville côtière pittoresque offrant une mer d'un bleu magnifique, des plages tranquilles et des bateaux de pêche colorés. Les bâtiments coloniaux délabrés rappellent que Cape Coast fut jadis une capitale coloniale européenne, passant entre les mains des Portugais, des Néerlandais, des Suédois, des Danois et des Britanniques au fil des siècles. Ceux qui survivaient à ces conditions étaient forcés de franchir la 'Porte du non-retour', une porte voûtée dotée de lourdes battants qui se refermaient derrière eux avant qu'ils ne soient forcés à monter à bord des navires négriers. 'Pour beaucoup, cette porte représente un voyage du connu vers l'inconnu', a expliqué Blankson. 'Et à partir de ce moment-là, on s'attendait à une résistance.' Alors que de nombreux touristes utilisent Cape Coast comme point de départ pour visiter d'autres attractions ghanéennes, comme le parc national de Kakum, la ville espère développer le tourisme des racines, en misant sur le château, afin d'encourager les séjours plus longs et les dépenses plus importantes. Ce chapitre sombre de l'histoire raconte non seulement une histoire de souffrance, mais aussi de survie. Blankson a noté qu'Obama était 'surpris, choqué et attristé, mais aussi motivé... car si les Noirs ont survécu à cela, cela témoigne de la résilience des êtres humains et d'un fort instinct de survie.'

article_content: Britain's fattest dog is on a crash diet because his owner kept forgetting he’d already been fed. Alfie, a labrador, weighed 12st 5lb (80kg) when the RSPCA took him in. That’s almost three times the normal weight of a labrador, and as heavy as Manchester United forward Wayne Rooney. It took four people using towels as slings to lift him when he arrived at the RSPCA’s Leybourne Animal Centre in Kent. Britain's former fattest dog, Alfie, weighed 12.5 stone last year - as much as Wayne Rooney - before arriving at the RSPCA's door for help. The 12-year-old canine was signed over to the RSPCA after his elderly owner repeatedly forgot he had already fed him. Christine Dooley, centre manager, said: 'He literally could not stand up when he arrived because he was so fat. I have never seen a dog that fat before in my 27 years with the RSPCA; he must be Britain’s fattest pet.' 'He was just a massive blob with a leg at each corner.' 'He was being fed to death; it’s amazing he was alive given his size. A healthy Labrador weighs about 30 kilos (4 stone 7lbs), so poor Alfie was carrying the weight of two Labradors and a Staffie too.' Alfie struggled to walk more than a few steps and could not even lift his legs a couple of inches into a raised bed in his kennel, so staff at the centre made him comfortable with a piece of carpet and blankets on the floor. Alfie's neck is so big he wears the same size collar as a St Bernard. Alfie was passed to the RSPCA after his elderly owner kept forgetting that he had already fed him. He has been put on a carefully calorie-controlled diet with two meals a day, weekly weigh-ins and strictly no treats. His obesity means he pants when he breathes, and he may have damaged his joints and suffered pressure sores on his legs. Since arriving at the centre in March this year, he has lost about four and a half stone. This means he is more than halfway to his target weight. Wayne Rooney weighs the same as Alfie. Christine said: 'When he first came in he couldn’t go on walks because of his size, but each day, as the weight comes off, he is able to take a few steps further. We have to be careful when staff take him for a walk because if he sits down and refuses to get back up, we have to call in extra people to lift him up again.' 'We want the weight to come off slowly to give his leg muscles a chance to build up strength and for his skin to shrink. We cannot foster him out yet because he wouldn’t be able to get him into the back of a car.' 'He’s such a lovely dog, and his tail never stops wagging; everyone here has fallen in love with him.' Once Alfie has reached a manageable weight, staff at the centre near Maidstone, Kent, will start looking for a home for him. His new owner will need to keep up his healthy diet and gentle exercise regime. Although Alfie’s obesity is extreme, it appears to be a growing problem among dogs. Since 2009, the number of complaints and calls the RSPCA has received about fat, obese and overweight dogs has steadily increased from about 20 a month to more than 30. RSPCA Inspector Caroline Doe, based in Kent, said overindulging a pet is just as harmful as not feeding them enough. She said: 'Alfie’s case is exceptional; I’ve never seen a dog that big before, but there are lots of dogs out there which are overweight or obese.' 'People don’t seem to realise it’s a problem because they think they are showing their pets love by giving them treats and titbits.' 'In fact, in terms of causing suffering, allowing your dog to become extremely obese is just as damaging as starving it and letting it get very skinny.'

L'inspectrice de la RSPCA, Caroline Doe, basée dans le Kent, a déclaré que le fait de trop gâter un animal de compagnie est tout aussi néfaste que de ne pas le nourrir suffisamment. 'Les gens ne semblent pas se rendre compte que c'est un problème parce qu'ils pensent qu'ils montrent leur amour à leurs animaux de compagnie en leur donnant des friandises et des amuse-gueules.' article_content: In Jakarta, Indonesia, CNN reports that a 14-year-old Australian boy may face jail time in Bali for alleged marijuana possession. The teenager, masked, entered a local court complex for his trial's first day on Tuesday, amidst a media throng. To reduce stress on the boy, prosecutor Gusti Gede Putu Atmaja stated the judge would not wear his customary robe. The trial is closed to the public. The Australian teen, whose name has not been released, is charged with violating Indonesia's stringent narcotics laws. The most serious charge, possession under article 111, carries a maximum sentence of six years. He is also charged with drug use under article 127, potentially resulting in a four-year sentence. Article 128, the least severe charge, concerns drug use by minors and considers their history of drug use. It does not carry criminal liability and could lead to rehabilitation instead of imprisonment. Mohammad Rifan, the teen's lawyer, stated, 'We are optimistic and hope he will be returned to his parents and avoid jail time.' However, the prosecutor emphasized that article 128 stipulates a minor's parents must report drug use to Indonesian authorities. Actions taken by guardians in his home country are not legally recognized in Indonesia. If a jail sentence is imposed, Atmaja suggested it might be 'as short as a few months,' potentially with credit for time served. The prosecution presented two witnesses at Tuesday's trial. Rifan anticipates a swift decision, with twice-weekly hearings possibly concluding by mid-November. Rifan noted the boy was stressed by media attention but was otherwise in relatively good condition during the hearing. His next court appearance is scheduled for Friday. He has been detained since his October 4 arrest for allegedly buying 3.6 grams of cannabis. He was vacationing with his parents in Bali, a popular tourist destination for Australians. Initially held at a police headquarters, he was recently moved to an immigration detention center. Despite intensive lobbying by Australian officials and his lawyer, prosecutors announced last week that the minor would stand trial. Indonesia's anti-drug laws are known to be strict. Visitors are warned upon arrival that certain drug crimes are punishable by death. Many have been arrested and convicted for various drug offenses. Currently, two Australians are on death row in Bali's Kerobokan prison, and six others are serving life sentences.

article_content: Tyrese Gibson, famed for his music and acting career, is venturing into new territory with his digital comic book series, 'Mayhem'. The 'Transformers' actor voices 'Mayhem,' a hero characterized as the 'embodiment of raw justice and vengeance.' Gibson has partnered with Apple to digitally develop 'Mayhem,' aiming to redefine the comic book experience. Gibson explains that his nontraditional approach stems from feeling limited by traditional paper comic books, emphasizing he's not a lifelong comic book reader. 'I felt [the traditional experience] was pretty limiting...'. 'So I set up this technology with my team, and this is the first-ever digital comic book [on iTunes] in the history of comic books,' says Gibson. The third issue of 'Mayhem,' available on iTunes, is the first to integrate interactive elements like sound effects, page transitions, and voiceovers, with Gibson himself voicing the main character. Gibson's foray exemplifies Hollywood's growing interest in comic books, highlighted by Walt Disney Studios' $4 billion acquisition of Marvel Entertainment. Following the success of comic-based films like 'Batman' and 'Iron Man,' a 'Mayhem' film isn't far-fetched. For now, Gibson is focused on establishing 'Mayhem'. Although he didn't disclose specific sales figures, he claimed worldwide sales would be impressive. CNN: What sparked your interest in comic books? Tyrese Gibson: I attended Comic-Con about a year ago to promote 'Death Race'. I was impressed by the fans' passion, regardless of how they appeared. 'I just love comic books,' they said. 'It was the first time I was ever exposed to that much selfless passion...'. That motivated me to be part of this world, leading to the creation of 'Mayhem'. CNN: What inspired the story of 'Mayhem'? Gibson: My partners Mike Lee, Will Wilson, and I brainstormed concepts, creating a unique ongoing series with cliffhangers that encourage readers to continue. CNN: As a newcomer, what feedback have you received from the comic book community? Gibson: There are always cynics who question your motives. I faced similar skepticism when transitioning between singing and acting. Some in the comic book world launched a smear campaign. 'Man, stick to singing; stick to acting.' I approached this innocently, wanting to share my love for comic books and promote digital innovation, which the comic book world hasn't fully embraced. So, I contacted my network and set up a meeting – this is my baby. CNN: How did artist Jim Lee get involved? Gibson: I found Jim Lee on Twitter and connected with him. CNN: What did you learn from him? Gibson: I learned so much. He educated me about key figures like Alan Moore and Grant Morrison, providing a comprehensive overview of the comic book world. CNN: Could 'Mayhem' become a film? Gibson: Currently, there are no discussions about a 'Mayhem' film. While we've been approached, my priority is building a solid fan base before considering a film adaptation. There's plenty of time for that.

article_content: Los Angeles, California (CNN) -- Television producer Stephen J. Cannell, renowned for his work on shows such as '21 Jump Street' and 'The A-Team,' passed away on Thursday, according to his publicist. Cannell was 69 years old. Cannell died at his home in Pasadena, California, from complications related to melanoma. He was surrounded by family and loved ones, according to a family statement. Beginning in the 1970s with 'The Rockford Files,' he created, wrote, and produced several iconic TV series. His other notable series included 'Greatest American Hero,' 'The A-Team,' 'Hunter,' 'Riptide,' 'Hardcastle & McCormick,' '21 Jump Street,' 'Wiseguy,' 'The Commish,' 'Profit,' and the syndicated shows 'Renegade' and 'Silk Stalkings.' Viewers may remember the trademark closing for Cannell's productions, where he was shown at a typewriter throwing a sheet of paper over his shoulder. He also acted, appearing in some of his own shows. Cannell had a recurring role on ABC-TV's series 'Castle.' Cannell authored 16 novels, including the 'Shane Scully' series. He is survived by his wife of 46 years, Marcia, his three children, and three grandchildren, the family stated. Having overcome severe dyslexia as a child growing up in Pasadena, Cannell later became a spokesman for the International Dyslexia Association and an advocate for children and adults with learning disabilities. He established an independent production company, Stephen J. Cannell Productions, in 1979, which allowed him control and ownership of his shows. His studio is currently developing feature film versions of several of his hit TV shows, including '21 Jump Street' and 'The Greatest American Hero.' The movie version of 'The A-Team' was released in theaters last summer. CNN's Jack Hannah contributed to this report.

article_content: Emily Allen reported on November 18, 2011, that a music teacher is striving to preserve a famous Yorkshire song, as most young people in the region are unfamiliar with it. The traditional folk song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at' – meaning 'on Ilkley Moor without a hat' – is considered a significant part of Yorkshire's heritage. Gordon Eddison, 55, from Otley, West Yorkshire, was surprised to find that very few children had even heard of the song. Gordon Eddison, who conducts the Otley Brass Band, is determined to re-introduce this traditional folk song to the region and has initiated a campaign to preserve it. Eddison recounted asking youngsters if they knew the song's words, and they either had no idea or, in one case, asked if the band Muse had recorded it. He emphasized the importance of preserving Yorkshire's heritage by ensuring young people know this song, preventing it from simply becoming words on a novelty tea towel. He urges parents and grandparents to teach children 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at,' highlighting the vital role singing plays in children’s musical and social education. Eddison estimates that only 10 percent of children are familiar with the song. He suspects parents and grandparents mistakenly believe the song is taught in schools. To illustrate his point, he took members of the Otley Brass Band to the Cow and Calf rocks on Ilkley Moor, believed to be where the lyrics were composed. Eddison hopes to encourage schools to teach the song and envisions an annual brass band competition on the moor to celebrate the tune, according to the Daily Telegraph. The song narrates a story of a lover courting Mary Jane on Ilkley Moor without a hat ('baht 'at'). The singer scolds the lover for not wearing a hat, as the cold winds of Ilkley Moor could lead to death from exposure. This, in turn, leads to burial, the eating of the corpse by worms, the consumption of the worms by ducks, and finally, the eating of the ducks by the singers.

article_content: A two-year-old boy died after his mother accidentally gave him liquid methadone, which she had stored in a Gatorade bottle, police reported. Aiden Goff died, and two of his siblings were hospitalized after their mother, Jill Goff, mistakenly served them the drug in a sippy cup at their home in Tooele, Utah, on Friday afternoon. Methadone is a pain reliever that can also be used to help recovering addicts manage withdrawal symptoms; its side effects can resemble those of heroin. Police believe she obtained the drug legally but have not explained why it was in liquid form or stored in a drink bottle. Police were called to the home at 6 p.m. on Friday after the 32-year-old mother found Aiden not breathing. Emergency responders tried to save him, but he was pronounced dead at the home. Later that evening, the boy's eight-year-old brother and five-year-old sister were taken to the emergency room and both tested positive for methadone, police told the Salt Lake Tribune. The boy had developed a rash, and his eyes were swollen, according to a probable cause statement. Both children survived. The hospitalized children told relatives and detectives that their mother had given Aiden a drink, but he didn't like it, the probable cause statement indicated. When he complained, the mother gave it to the five-year-old, who agreed it was disgusting. The eight-year-old then tasted it and said it tasted like medicine, the Tribune reported. After realizing her mistake, Jill Goff put Aiden down for a nap, but he did not wake up. 'The children told us there was a sippy cup passed around between the three of them that mom had prepared for them, and it didn’t taste right,' Tooele Police Captain Paul Wimmer told KSL. Investigators believe that she inadvertently gave him methadone, which had been stored in the Gatorade bottle, instead of Gatorade, Wimmer said. The mother then realized she had switched the liquids and tried to induce vomiting in her two-year-old son, the statement said. She then gave him a bath and put him down for a nap. She told investigators that she did not call police because she was scared. A 14-year-old sibling went to wake Aiden, but he was unresponsive. Goff called 911. She was arrested on suspicion of homicide, two counts of child abuse, and endangerment of a child or vulnerable adult. She remained in the Tooele County jail. Police said Goff has no prior record, and they believe she did not intend to kill her son. 'While we don’t have any evidence that suggests that she was trying to harm the children, a certain level of care is required with such a dangerous substance and medication,' Wimmer said. Her husband, Cody, described her as a loving mother, Fox 13 reported. The four other children—aged 5, 8, 11, and 14—have been placed with relatives. Facebook images show her doting on the five children and proudly posing with Aiden. 'I want to let you all know my baby boy Aiden Goff passed away in his momma's arms tonight,' she wrote on her Facebook page on Friday.

article_content: Amanda Williams reported on November 8, 2013, about a new iPhone app that helps parents monitor their child's temperature. This app uses a thermometer that connects to the phone's audio jack to take temperature readings. The app displays the temperature and provides a chart of possible symptoms to assist users in self-diagnosing. The thermometer app also keeps records of health issues and offers users an 'illness forecast,' estimating recovery time and contagiousness. Additionally, users can compare symptoms with others nearby to identify local health trends. The Kinsa Smart Thermometer was created by Inder Singh, who was inspired after struggling to find helpful information online when he had a lung infection. Singh stated that he wanted to 'revolutionize the world's most common medical device' because 'fever is an early sign of illness.' He aims to collect data on fever outbreaks to benefit whole populations, explaining that he wanted to 'engage people who had just fallen ill in a conversation' to provide information and 'collect information to map health,' as he told eWeek. He added that by using mobile devices intelligently, they are creating simpler, smarter, connected devices that will be available at or below the current cost of these products. Singh believes that thermometers like theirs will eventually become the norm.

article_content: In Vermont, authorities have charged the uncle of Brooke Bennett, a missing 12-year-old, with sexual assault of a minor. However, they clarified that this charge is not connected to his niece's disappearance. According to police reports, the inquiry into Brooke Bennett's disappearance led to evidence suggesting that her uncle had sexually assaulted someone else. Michael Jacques, aged 42, now faces charges of aggravated sexual assault against a minor, a crime that could result in a prison sentence ranging from 10 years to life. Jacques is listed as a registered sex offender in Vermont. Vermont State Police Col. James Baker indicated on Monday that investigators are exploring the possibility that Jacques may have additional victims of sexual abuse. Col. Baker urged any child or teenager who might have had contact with Michael Jacques to come forward and speak with the state police. Authorities began to concentrate on Jacques based on data obtained through computer forensics, Baker noted, adding that the case highlights the dangers associated with social networking online. Baker refrained from commenting on the family dynamics between Brooke and her uncle. Law enforcement officials have stated that prior to her disappearance, Brooke was communicating with an individual through an online social networking site. Investigators have since been examining her computer. An affidavit from State Police Detective Sgt. William Jenkins reveals that the girl Jacques is accused of assaulting told investigators that around the age of 9 or 10, she received a telephone call and a note stating she was selected for a 'program for sex' and that Jacques was to serve as her trainer, The Associated Press reported. The AP further stated that the girl reported being informed that she and two other girls were part of this program. 'The first who does it lives and the second gets her throat cut,' the affidavit detailed. Brooke went missing last Wednesday after a visit to a convenience store in Randolph, Vermont, officials reported. Several days later, law enforcement announced the discovery of clothing items believed to belong to her. Brooke's disappearance prompted the issuance of Vermont's first Amber Alert, officials confirmed. Her father, James Bennett, has made a plea for any information concerning his daughter's whereabouts, expressing his distress and emphasizing his desire for her safe return home. He told WCAX-TV, a CNN affiliate, 'Obviously I'm upset... We just want her home. We want her back.' Police have stated they are unsure if Brooke willingly left with someone.

article_content: It's often said that appearances can be deceiving, but the origin of all the world's gold could be linked to extreme cosmic events that release intense light into space. Recent research offers support for the idea that gold is formed from colliding neutron stars. 'These collisions could explain the total amount of gold found in the universe,' stated Edo Berger, an astronomer from the Harvard-Smithson Center for Astrophysics. Berger presented these findings, which are under consideration for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, at a press conference on Wednesday. Neutron stars are the remnant cores of stars that previously exploded as supernovae. According to studies, the neutron stars involved in the event studied by Berger and his team were about the size of Boston, yet contained about 1.5 times the mass of our sun. When these neutron stars, which were orbiting each other, collided at great speed, they produced a black hole. The combined mass of the neutron stars was too great, causing the resulting object to collapse into a black hole. Stan Woosley, an astronomer at the University of California, Santa Cruz, who was not part of the research, explained that gravitational radiation causes neutron stars to collide by draining energy from their orbits. He described each of these star cores as a massive atomic nucleus in an email. 'Smashing two of these together at near light speed is sure to create an impressive spectacle,' Woosley remarked. Berger and his fellow researchers observed a brief gamma-ray burst, which they believe resulted from a neutron star collision. This burst is a surge of high-energy light; this one was deemed 'short duration' because it lasted less than two-tenths of a second. This burst occurred 3.9 billion light-years away from Earth, a significant distance; however, it's among the nearest gamma-ray bursts that scientists have observed. The gamma-ray burst left a glow containing considerable infrared light. Scientists believe that radioactive elements, created as the merging neutron stars ejected material, emitted this light as they underwent radioactive decay. Woosley explained that decay heats the expelled matter. This infrared glow provided scientists with a valuable opportunity. It gave scientists confirmation that short gamma-ray bursts can be traced back to neutron star collisions. 'This provides solid evidence linking a short gamma-ray burst to the collision of two neutron stars,' Berger stated. Woosley noted that there is still a possibility that the particular infrared light that the scientists detected was not caused by radioactive decay but by a different light produced in conjunction with the gamma-ray burst. However, he says that the theory of gold being formed in neutron star collisions is 'almost certainly accurate.' Although it has been suggested that gold originates from supernova explosions, Berger stated that simulations indicate that it's difficult to produce gold in that way. Supernovae may contribute some gold to the universe, but neutron star collisions appear to be the primary process for producing gold. Scientists hypothesize that the material ejected by the merging neutron stars included a substantial amount of gold. Berger estimates that a mass of gold equivalent to 10 moons is created and ejected when two neutron stars merge. At today's market value, this would be approximately 10 octillion dollars. Platinum and uranium also result from this collision process, according to Woosley. All of these elements circulate between stars in a gaseous form and eventually integrate into subsequent generations of stars, like our sun. Woosley stated, 'The gold and platinum in our rings, as well as the uranium in our bombs and reactors, are small pieces of neutron stars that merged in our galaxy long before the sun was formed.' This same space-borne gold became part of the formation of Earth and the rest of the solar system, including the sun. Gold present during Earth's formation sank to its core. However, we have gold that is accessible for mining closer to the planet's surface, because meteorites delivered it later, according to a 2011 study in the journal Nature. More than 200 million years after Earth was formed, a shower of meteorites hit the planet, carrying gold that remained in the mantle. The next time you wear a gold wedding band or another piece of jewelry, consider its fascinating cosmic origin.

Lorsque ces étoiles à neutrons, qui étaient en orbite l'une autour de l'autre, sont entrées en collision à grande vitesse, elles ont produit un trou noir. La masse combinée des étoiles à neutrons était trop importante, ce qui a entraîné l'effondrement de l'objet résultant en un trou noir. Stan Woosley, astronome à l'Université de Californie, Santa Cruz, qui ne faisait pas partie de la recherche, a expliqué que le rayonnement gravitationnel provoque la collision des étoiles à neutrons en drainant l'énergie de leurs orbites. Il a décrit chacun de ces cœurs d'étoile comme un noyau atomique massif dans un e-mail. 'Frapper deux de ces objets ensemble à une vitesse proche de celle de la lumière est sûr de créer un spectacle impressionnant', a fait remarquer Woosley. Berger et ses collègues chercheurs ont observé un bref sursaut gamma, qui, selon eux, résultait d'une collision d'étoiles à neutrons. Ce sursaut est une décharge de lumière de haute énergie ; celui-ci a été jugé 'de courte durée' car il a duré moins de deux dixièmes de seconde. Ce sursaut s'est produit à 3,9 milliards d'années-lumière de la Terre, une distance importante ; cependant, il fait partie des sursauts gamma les plus proches que les scientifiques aient observés. Le sursaut gamma a laissé une lueur contenant une quantité considérable de lumière infrarouge. Les scientifiques pensent que les éléments radioactifs, créés lorsque les étoiles à neutrons en fusion ont éjecté de la matière, ont émis cette lumière lors de leur désintégration radioactive. Woosley a expliqué que la désintégration chauffe la matière expulsée. Cette lueur infrarouge a fourni aux scientifiques une précieuse opportunité. Elle a donné aux scientifiques la confirmation que les sursauts gamma courts peuvent être attribués à des collisions d'étoiles à neutrons. 'Cela fournit des preuves solides reliant un sursaut gamma court à la collision de deux étoiles à neutrons', a déclaré Berger. Woosley a noté qu'il existe toujours une possibilité que la lumière infrarouge particulière que les scientifiques ont détectée n'ait pas été causée par la désintégration radioactive, mais par une lumière différente produite en conjonction avec le sursaut gamma. Cependant, il affirme que la théorie de la formation de l'or lors des collisions d'étoiles à neutrons est 'presque certainement exacte'. Bien qu'il ait été suggéré que l'or provient d'explosions de supernova, Berger a déclaré que les simulations indiquent qu'il est difficile de produire de l'or de cette manière. Les supernovas peuvent contribuer à une certaine quantité d'or dans l'univers, mais les collisions d'étoiles à neutrons semblent être le principal processus de production d'or. Les scientifiques émettent l'hypothèse que la matière éjectée par les étoiles à neutrons en fusion comprenait une quantité substantielle d'or. Berger estime qu'une masse d'or équivalente à 10 lunes est créée et éjectée lorsque deux étoiles à neutrons fusionnent. À la valeur marchande actuelle, cela représenterait environ 10 octillions de dollars. Le platine et l'uranium résultent également de ce processus de collision, selon Woosley. Tous ces éléments circulent entre les étoiles sous forme gazeuse et finissent par s'intégrer aux générations d'étoiles suivantes, comme notre soleil. Woosley a déclaré : 'L'or et le platine de nos bagues, ainsi que l'uranium de nos bombes et de nos réacteurs, sont de petits morceaux d'étoiles à neutrons qui ont fusionné dans notre galaxie bien avant la formation du soleil.' Ce même or d'origine spatiale a participé à la formation de la Terre et du reste du système solaire, y compris le soleil. L'or présent lors de la formation de la Terre a coulé vers son noyau. Cependant, nous avons de l'or qui est accessible à l'extraction plus près de la surface de la planète, car des météorites l'ont apporté plus tard, selon une étude de 2011 dans la revue Nature. Plus de 200 millions d'années après la formation de la Terre, une pluie de météorites a frappé la planète, transportant de l'or qui est resté dans le manteau. La prochaine fois que vous porterez une alliance en or ou un autre bijou, pensez à sa fascinante origine cosmique.

article_content: Kerry Kennedy, daughter of the late Senator Robert F. Kennedy and former spouse of New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, might testify Wednesday in her defense regarding her 2012 DWI trial, stemming from a traffic incident. Kennedy faces a misdemeanor charge for allegedly driving while intoxicated, linked to a July 2012 incident where she reportedly swerved across lanes and collided with a tractor-trailer on a Westchester County, New York, interstate. Testimony indicates Kennedy left the crash site despite tire damage and was later found slumped over her Lexus SUV's steering wheel. Kennedy claims she took a pill around 7:30 a.m. that day, believing it was her thyroid medication, but may have mistaken it for zolpidem, a strong sleep aid. Trial testimony confirmed zolpidem's presence in her system via a blood test. As her defense began Tuesday, Kennedy's sister, Rory Kennedy, spoke of their close relationship, stating, "She's truly my closest friend." Asked about Kerry's trustworthiness, Rory said she wrote 'Speak Truth to Power,' reflecting her lifelong commitment to justice and honesty. Supporters, including sister Kathleen Kennedy Townsend, brothers Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Douglas Kennedy, and family matriarch Ethel Kennedy, have attended the Westchester County trial. Earlier Tuesday, Bradley Molloy, a New York State Police drug-detection expert, testified that Kennedy passed roadside sobriety tests well three hours after initially failing them. Molloy stated he suspected a medical issue caused Kennedy's accident and disorientation, finding no signs of intoxication. Kennedy also expressed concern about her blood sample from Northern Westchester Hospital, saying, "She was worried and wanted to understand what had occurred," according to Molloy. Kennedy was hospitalized overnight for observation. Assistant District Attorney Stefanie DeNise argued Monday that even if Kennedy, 54, unintentionally took the sleep aid, she was responsible for safely pulling over. Defense attorney Gerald Lefcourt countered that Kennedy had no time to react, stating, "The zolpidem activates, incapacitates her, and she enters a state of 'sleep driving.'" Tuesday afternoon, Kennedy's defense debated the drug's effects with expert witness Elizabeth Pratt, a laboratory director, who admitted zolpidem is "a very powerful, fast-acting hypnotic" that impairs cognitive and motor skills within 15-45 minutes. Pratt testified zolpidem's impact on Kerry Kennedy would have peaked around 9 a.m., about when Kennedy initially failed sobriety tests after a 911 call. Prosecutor Doreen Lloyd asked Pratt if zolpidem is a "knock-out pill," and Pratt said it needs time to enter the bloodstream and brain. Lloyd then asked if a person retains brain function and decision-making ability before the drug takes effect, to which Pratt replied, "Yes." The trial resumes Wednesday at 9:30 a.m.

article_content: The Forestry Commission has announced a national emergency after detecting ash dieback, a destructive disease affecting ash trees across Europe, in the British countryside. This outbreak, discovered in East Anglia, raises concerns that it could cause damage reminiscent of the Dutch elm disease crisis in the 1970s. In response, the government plans to implement a ban on ash tree imports and impose stricter regulations on ash tree movement within the UK starting Monday. The disease is caused by the Chalara fraxinea fungus, which leads to leaf loss, crown dieback, and eventually, the death of the tree. This fungus decimated 90% of Denmark's ash trees in just seven years. Previously identified in nurseries and newly planted areas like car parks and college campuses, the Forestry Commission is now treating the fungus as a quarantine pest and urging the public to report any suspected cases under national emergency protocols. Environment Secretary Owen Paterson informed MPs about these measures following a question from Simon Hart, a Tory MP, regarding the department's strategy to manage the disease. Paterson acknowledged the 'horrific danger' to the UK's ash trees. Dame Joan Ruddock, a Labour MP, criticized the timing of the government's response, suggesting a ban on ash seedling imports should have occurred sooner. She emphasized that any delay would be unforgivable given the public's value of ash trees. The Woodland Trust has confirmed the presence of the fungus on their estate in Suffolk and supports the import and movement ban. The Horticultural Trades Association also encourages its members to voluntarily halt ash tree imports. However, concerns remain about the limited effectiveness of an import ban if the disease is already widespread. Andrew Sharkey of the Woodland Trust warned that losing ash trees, which constitute about 30% of the UK's wooded areas, would severely impact the country's ecology. The Trust has requested the government to form an emergency summit or taskforce to address tree diseases. Dr. John Morgan from the Forestry Commission stated that efforts to combat the disease have been intensified, including redeployment of staff to survey woodlands. He also noted that the East Anglia outbreak might be isolated and urged the public to report suspected cases and consult the Forestry Commission's website for more information. The Commission is also suspending ash tree planting in public forests. Infected ash trees have been found at the Norfolk Wildlife Trust’s Lower Wood reserve, prompting the trust to work closely with the Forestry Commission's plant health team. However, the trust’s head of nature reserves, John Milton, indicated that identifying the disease's true extent might be challenging due to the upcoming leaf fall. The Forestry Commission has provided a pictorial guide to assist in identifying the signs of ash dieback.

article_content: A remarkably well-preserved example of a fossilized marine creature is set to fetch £100,000 at auction. The 6ft long ichthyosaur was discovered by a fossil hunter at low tide after rough seas tore away a section of cliff. The unnamed fossil enthusiast worked tirelessly for three days to collect the 200 million-year-old remains before expected storms would have ultimately destroyed them. The 6ft long ichthyosaur (pictured) was uncovered in the late 1990s and is now up for auction. The beasts would have looked similar to dolphins but were reptilian. He removed sections of rock from the cliffs known as Black Ven, near Lyme Regis, Dorset, and took them to local preparator Chris Moore. Mr. Moore then spent hundreds of hours chipping away at the rock to expose the fossilized bones of the ichthyosaur. The result is one of the most impressive examples ever found, with the ichthyosaur in the same leaping position as when it died. Remarkably, one of its paddles is preserved in 3D, protruding from its body at an angle of 45 degrees. Ichthyosaurs - literally meaning 'fish-lizards' - were giant marine reptiles that resembled dolphins and thrived during much of the Mesozoic era. These huge animals rapidly diversified from being lizards with fins to developing a much more streamlined, fish-like form built for speed. One species has been calculated to have a cruising speed of 22mph (36 km/h). They first appeared approximately 245 million years ago and at least one species survived until about 90 million years ago. The reptiles were particularly abundant in the Jurassic Period, until they were replaced as the top aquatic predators by another reptilian order, the plesiosaurs, in the Cretaceous Period. The specimen, which was uncovered in the late 1990s, is now being offered for sale at Summers Place Auctions in Billingshurst, West Sussex. While it has a pre-sale estimate of 80,000 pounds, it is expected to fetch around £100,000, according to initial estimates. Errol Fuller, a natural history expert and curator for the auction, said: 'When you find fossils like this one, they aren’t in the state that you now see.' 'A lot of the bone is covered in rock, probably in three or four very solid lumps, and the finder would have had to use a wheelbarrow or something to remove it.' 'It had been exposed on a ledge by rough tides, and had the fossil hunter not found it, it could have been washed away and broken up very quickly.' 'The fossil was prepared by Chris Moore at his workshop in Charmouth. The rock had to be drilled away very carefully; it is a painstakingly slow process.' 'We are talking about a huge amount of work that has gone into preparing it.' Ichthyosaurs (CGI pictured) were giant marine reptiles that resembled dolphins and thrived during much of the Mesozoic era. 'It is complete and in a beautiful state of preservation and has been very well prepared.” Ichthyosaurs swam in the sea at the same time dinosaurs roamed the land, which was around 220 to 65 million years ago. The beasts would have looked similar to dolphins but were reptilian. Mary Anning, born in 1799 in Lyme Regis, helped extract a complete ichthyosaur when she was just 12 years old. The ichthyosaur is being sold on November 27.

'Le fossile a été préparé par Chris Moore dans son atelier à Charmouth. La roche a dû être dégagée avec une grande minutie ; c'est un travail de longue haleine.' 'Nous parlons d'une quantité de travail considérable pour arriver à ce résultat.' Les ichtyosaures (dont on voit ici une reconstitution numérique) étaient de grands reptiles marins qui ressemblaient à des dauphins et ont prospéré pendant une grande partie de l'ère mésozoïque. 'Il est complet, magnifiquement conservé et a été préparé avec un grand soin.' Les ichtyosaures nageaient dans la mer à la même époque où les dinosaures peuplaient la terre, soit il y a environ 220 à 65 millions d'années. Ces créatures ressemblaient à des dauphins, mais étaient en réalité des reptiles. Mary Anning, née en 1799 à Lyme Regis, a contribué à l'extraction d'un ichtyosaure complet alors qu'elle n'avait que 12 ans. La vente de l'ichtyosaure aura lieu le 27 novembre.

article_content: Responding to increasing consumer aversion towards artificial additives, Panera has announced its intention to eliminate artificial colors, flavors, sweeteners, and preservatives from its entire menu by 2016. This decision is a central component of its newly introduced 'Food Policy', which emphasizes a commitment to 'clean' and 'simple' ingredients. The bakery-cafe chain, which operates roughly 1,800 locations across the United States, is implementing this policy amidst a period of decelerated sales growth. Panera Bread Co. hopes to revitalize its business by changing their ordering system and switching to daytime baking hours to cultivate a more inviting atmosphere. The launch of Panera's 'Food Policy' highlights the marketing advantage of branding foods as natural, irrespective of actual nutritional advantages. Customers are drawn to foods they perceive as natural because they often feel less guilt about their caloric intake. Chipotle's popularity, for example, has been partially attributed to its image as a healthier option compared to conventional fast-food restaurants like McDonald's. Similarly, Subway recently discontinued the use of azodicarbonamide, an ingredient also found in yoga mats, following a public petition. Panera, based in St. Louis, reports it is halfway through removing artificial ingredients from its menu. The company continues to seek alternatives for artificial colors and preservatives, especially in products such as bakery icings. Additives slated for removal include specific artificial coloring agents and preservatives. However, labeling foods as natural or free of artificial ingredients can expose companies to scrutiny and even lawsuits. Whole Foods Market is currently facing a lawsuit alleging the use of numerous artificial ingredients in its store-brand products, despite its 'nothing artificial' claim. Panera also intends to continue using genetically modified ingredients (GMOs), differentiating itself from Chipotle, which aims to eliminate GMOs entirely. Neither Panera nor Chipotle plans to stop selling fountain sodas from Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, even though these beverages contain high fructose corn syrup. CEO Ron Shaich mentioned that Panera's commitment to sourcing chicken raised without antibiotics ten years ago significantly increased sales. Panera's new food policy emphasizes transparency by providing easy access to information regarding ingredients and nutritional content. It also affirms its commitment to positively influencing the food system by supporting North American suppliers whenever possible. Whether this new policy will boost customer numbers remains to be seen. Panera experienced a 2.6 percent sales increase at company-owned locations open for at least a year, a decline from 6.5 percent in 2012 and 4.9 percent in 2011. The company projects sales growth of 2 to 3.5 percent this year. In line with growing trend, several other chains, including Chipotle and Starbucks, are also working to reduce artificial additives. Ron Shaich, Panera's founder and CEO, stated 'We decided it was time to put all this into a clear and concise policy'.

Panera Bread Co. espère relancer ses activités en modifiant son système de commande et en passant à des heures de cuisson diurnes afin de créer une atmosphère plus invitante. Le lancement de la 'Politique Alimentaire' de Panera met en évidence l'avantage marketing de présenter les aliments comme naturels, indépendamment des avantages nutritionnels réels. Les clients sont attirés par les aliments qu'ils perçoivent comme naturels, car ils se sentent souvent moins coupables de leur apport calorique. La popularité de Chipotle, par exemple, a été partiellement attribuée à son image d'option plus saine par rapport aux restaurants de restauration rapide classiques comme McDonald's. De même, Subway a récemment cessé d'utiliser l'azodicarbonamide, un ingrédient également présent dans les tapis de yoga, à la suite d'une pétition publique. Panera, basée à Saint-Louis, indique qu'elle a déjà supprimé la moitié des ingrédients artificiels de son menu. L'entreprise continue de rechercher des alternatives aux colorants et conservateurs artificiels, notamment dans les produits tels que les glaçages de boulangerie. Les additifs qui doivent être supprimés comprennent des agents colorants et des conservateurs artificiels spécifiques. Cependant, l'étiquetage des aliments comme naturels ou exempts d'ingrédients artificiels peut exposer les entreprises à un examen minutieux, voire à des poursuites judiciaires. Whole Foods Market fait actuellement l'objet d'une poursuite alléguant l'utilisation de nombreux ingrédients artificiels dans ses produits de marque maison, malgré son affirmation selon laquelle ils ne contiennent 'rien d'artificiel'. Panera a également l'intention de continuer à utiliser des ingrédients génétiquement modifiés (OGM), se différenciant ainsi de Chipotle, qui vise à éliminer complètement les OGM. Le PDG Ron Shaich a mentionné que l'engagement de Panera, il y a dix ans, à s'approvisionner en poulet élevé sans antibiotiques avait considérablement augmenté les ventes. La nouvelle politique alimentaire de Panera met l'accent sur la transparence en fournissant un accès facile aux informations concernant les ingrédients et la valeur nutritionnelle. Elle affirme également son engagement à avoir un impact positif sur le système alimentaire en soutenant les fournisseurs nord-américains dans la mesure du possible. Il reste à voir si cette nouvelle politique permettra d'augmenter le nombre de clients. Panera a enregistré une augmentation de 2,6 % de ses ventes dans les établissements appartenant à l'entreprise et ouverts depuis au moins un an, ce qui représente une baisse par rapport aux 6,5 % de 2012 et aux 4,9 % de 2011. L'entreprise prévoit une croissance des ventes de 2 à 3,5 % cette année. Conformément à la tendance croissante, plusieurs autres chaînes, dont Chipotle et Starbucks, s'efforcent également de réduire les additifs artificiels. Ron Shaich, fondateur et PDG de Panera, a déclaré : 'Nous avons décidé qu'il était temps de traduire tout cela dans une politique claire et concise'.

article_content: Recalling her father brings tears to Senna's eyes. 'I cried and I cried,' says Senna, now 14, as she remembers the day he passed away. Senna lives in La Rinconada, Peru. Her father died after years of working in the town's mines. He never had the opportunity to attend school, but he dreamed of becoming an engineer, a dream he passed on to his daughter. It is his words that give her strength today. 'Don't be like me,' he would tell her. 'Make something better of yourself, Senna. Study.' However, like everything else in La Rinconada, getting an education is a struggle. This mining town, home to approximately 30,000 people, sits at an altitude of three miles, making it the highest city in the world. Living conditions are challenging. In addition to the altitude, the town lacks running water and a sewage system. 'Education is a very low priority. There are no laws, no police, no one ensuring that children are attending school,' explains Maria Arana, writer for 'Girl Rising.' In the Puno province, where La Rinconada is located, nearly 68% of the population lives below the poverty line. The men work in the mines, while the women sell goods, search for gold in discarded mine rocks, or earn money through prostitution. 'This is no place for children,' Senna says. Even when schools are available, many parents need their children's help with work. 'If a mother is mashing rock, she may need assistance,' Arana notes. 'There are no rules in La Rinconada.' According to CARE, almost 29% of indigenous children in Peru do not attend school. But CARE is striving to change this. In 2003, the aid organization began working in La Rinconada to educate people about the importance of formal education and the dangers of child labor. Currently, over 23,000 children receive assistance at the kindergarten, elementary, and high school levels. Senna is one of these students and is now on track to achieve something that no one else in her family has accomplished: going to college. 'I have several dreams. I would like to study marketing, law, and engineering, but more than anything, I want to be a poet—a great poet.'

J'aimerais étudier le marketing, le droit et l'ingénierie, mais plus que tout, je veux être poète, une grande poète.'
